15.english_meaning: The total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
15.hindi_meaning: सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (एक निश्चित अवधि में देश के भीतर उत्पादित सभी वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल मूल्य)
15.example: The country's Gross Domestic Product grew significantly over the last fiscal year.

15.english_meaning: Distinct parts or branches of a nation's economy, such as agriculture, industry, and services.
15.hindi_meaning: क्षेत्र (अर्थव्यवस्था के विभिन्न भाग जैसे कृषि, उद्योग और सेवा क्षेत्र)
15.example: The economy is generally divided into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors.

15.english_meaning: Values or statistics that give an idea of the state or condition of something.
15.hindi_meaning: सूचक या संकेतक (किसी स्थिति को मापने के आंकड़े या पैमाना)
15.example: Literacy rate and life expectancy are important indicators of human development.

15.english_meaning: A process of enlarging people's choices and raising their level of well-being and education.
15.hindi_meaning: मानव विकास (लोगों के विकल्पों को बढ़ाने और उनके जीवन स्तर, स्वास्थ्य और शिक्षा में सुधार की प्रक्रिया)
15.example: Human development focuses on improving the quality of human life rather than just economic growth.

15.english_meaning: Carefully designed plans or methods to achieve a particular long-term goal.
15.hindi_meaning: रणनीति (किसी दीर्घकालिक लक्ष्य को प्राप्त करने के लिए बनाई गई योजनाएं)
15.example: Development strategies must address poverty and unemployment directly.

15.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone, or estimating its value and progress.
15.hindi_meaning: मूल्यांकन या समीक्षा (किसी कार्य, नीति या प्रगति की जांच और आकलन)
15.example: An appraisal of past economic policies helps in planning better future strategies.

15.english_meaning: An alphabetical list of terms or words relating to a specific subject, text, or dialect with their definitions.
15.hindi_meaning: शब्दकोश या शब्दावली (पाठ्यपुस्तक में दिए गए कठिन शब्दों और उनके अर्थों की सूची)
15.example: You can check the glossary at the back of the book for the meanings of technical terms.

15.english_meaning: An act of printing a book, article, or document again, usually with minor or no revisions.
15.hindi_meaning: पुनर्मुद्रण (किसी पुस्तक या दस्तावेज को दोबारा छापना)
15.example: This textbook is a revised reprint for the academic session.

15.english_meaning: The process of growing, changing, or advancing to a more advanced or beneficial state.
15.hindi_meaning: विकास (किसी व्यवस्था या समाज की प्रगति और सुधार की प्रक्रिया)
15.example: Sustainable development ensures that future generations can meet their needs.

15.english_meaning: Relating to the economy, or the wealth and resources of a country or region.
15.hindi_meaning: आर्थिक (देश की अर्थव्यवस्था, धन और संसाधनों से संबंधित)
15.example: Economic reforms in 1991 transformed India's trade policies.

15.english_meaning: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, or business.
15.hindi_meaning: नीति (सरकार या संगठन द्वारा लिया गया निर्णय या कार्य-योजना)
15.example: The government announced a new industrial policy to attract foreign investment.

15.english_meaning: Money received, especially on a regular basis, for work or through investments.
15.hindi_meaning: आय (काम, व्यवसाय या निवेश के जरिए प्राप्त होने वाला धन)
15.example: National income is a crucial measure to determine a country's standard of living.

16.english_meaning: A body of fundamental principles or established precedents according to which a state or other organization is acknowledged to be governed.
16.example: Every citizen of India must respect the Constitution.

16.english_meaning: To accept or act in accordance with a rule, decision, or recommendation.
16.example: We must abide by the laws made by the government.

16.english_meaning: The authority of a state to govern itself or another state.
16.example: It is our duty to protect the sovereignty and integrity of India.

16.english_meaning: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; the state of being whole and undivided.
16.example: National integration strengthens the unity and integrity of the country.

16.english_meaning: The state of being in agreement or peaceful coexistence.
16.example: People of all religions live in harmony in our town.

16.english_meaning: Going beyond the limits of; surpassing.
16.example: True friendship transcends all barriers of caste and creed.

16.english_meaning: Showing a critical or disrespectful attitude; disparaging.
16.example: We should renounce practices that are derogatory to women.

16.english_meaning: Valued objects and qualities such as cultural traditions, historic buildings, and countryside that have been passed down from previous generations.
16.example: We must preserve our rich cultural heritage for future generations.

16.english_meaning: Pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others, including animals.
16.example: We should always show compassion for living creatures.

16.english_meaning: A state of mind; here, a scientific outlook characterized by reason, questioning, and objectivity.
16.example: Education helps in developing a scientific temper among students.

16.english_meaning: Solemnly renounce (a belief, cause, or claim).
16.example: Citizens have a duty to safeguard public property and abjure violence.

16.english_meaning: An earnest and industrious attempt, effort, or undertaking.
16.example: Success in any endeavour requires hard work and dedication.

17.english_meaning: A political, economic, and cultural organisation of countries located in South-east Asia.
17.hindi_meaning: दक्षिण-पूर्व एशियाई राष्ट्रों का संघ - दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया में स्थित देशों का एक राजनीतिक, आर्थिक और सांस्कृतिक संगठन।
17.example: India often collaborates with ASEAN nations to enhance regional trade.

17.english_meaning: A statistical statement summarising all external transactions of a country over a period of time.
17.hindi_meaning: भुगतान संतुलन - एक निश्चित समयावधि में किसी देश के सभी बाहरी लेन-देन (प्राप्तियों और भुगतानों) का सारांश देने वाला सांख्यिकीय विवरण।
17.example: A deficit in the balance of payments can cause economic instability.

17.english_meaning: Factors that make it difficult or disadvantageous for new entrants to enter an established industry.
17.hindi_meaning: प्रवेश की बाधाएं - वे कारक जो नए उद्यमों के लिए पहले से स्थापित उद्योग में प्रवेश करना कठिन या अलाभकारी बनाते हैं।
17.example: High capital requirements act as major barriers to entry in the telecommunications sector.

17.english_meaning: The act of obeying or conforming to rules, regulations, or government laws.
17.hindi_meaning: अनुपालन - सरकारी नियमों, विनियमों या कानूनों का पालन करना।
17.example: Strict compliance with tax laws is mandatory for all registered businesses.

17.hindi_meaning: द्विपक्षीय - दो देशों या पक्षों के बीच होने वाला।
17.example: The two nations signed bilateral trade agreements to boost agricultural exports.

17.english_meaning: An official group of people entrusted with a specific duty or to study a particular problem.
17.hindi_meaning: आयोग - किसी विशिष्ट कार्य को करने या अध्ययन करने के लिए नियुक्त लोगों का आधिकारिक समूह।
17.example: The Brundtland Commission was established to study global environmental problems.

17.english_meaning: Economic development that is conducted without depletion of natural resources for future generations.
17.hindi_meaning: सतत विकास - भावी पीढ़ियों के संसाधनों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना किया जाने वाला विकास।
17.example: Sustainable development balances economic growth with environmental protection.

17.english_meaning: A situation where a government's total expenditures exceed its total income and tax receipts.
17.hindi_meaning: बजटीय घाटा - एक ऐसी स्थिति जब सरकार की कुल आय और कर प्राप्तियां उसके खर्चों से कम रह जाती हैं।
17.example: The government adopted measures to control the rising budgetary deficit.

17.english_meaning: The preservation, protection, or restoration of the natural environment and resources.
17.hindi_meaning: संरक्षण - प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण और संसाधनों की सुरक्षा और उनका समुचित उपयोग।
17.example: Energy conservation helps reduce electricity waste across different sectors.

17.english_meaning: Obtaining goods or services from an outside or foreign supplier, especially in place of an internal source.
17.hindi_meaning: आउटसोर्सिंग - किसी कंपनी द्वारा अपने व्यावसायिक कार्यों को किसी बाहरी या अन्य कंपनी से करवाना।
17.example: Many global firms rely on business process outsourcing to reduce operational costs.

17.english_meaning: An act or course of action to which a person or country is morally or legally bound; a duty or commitment.
17.hindi_meaning: दायित्व / देयताएँ - कानूनी या नैतिक रूप से पूरा करने योग्य कर्तव्य या जिम्मेदारियां।
17.example: The country must fulfill its financial obligations as per international agreements.

17.english_meaning: An instance of buying or exchanging something, especially an exchange of money or business activity.
17.hindi_meaning: लेन-देन - वस्तुओं, सेवाओं या धन का आदान-प्रदान।
17.example: All external transactions are carefully recorded in the country's balance of payments.

18.english_meaning: The maximum number of people or species that a specific environment can sustainably support indefinitely without environmental degradation.
18.hindi_meaning: वहन क्षमता - किसी पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र की वह अधिकतम सीमा जो बिना किसी क्षति के किसी जनसंख्या या प्रजाति का निरंतर भरण-पोषण कर सके।
18.example: Overpopulation can severely strain the carrying capacity of local natural resources.

18.english_meaning: A situation where a tax imposition leads to a disproportionate and cumulative rise in final prices.
18.hindi_meaning: क्रमिक प्रभाव - कर लगाने के कारण कीमतों में अनुपातहीन और लगातार होने वाली अत्यधिक वृद्धि।
18.example: The cascading effect of multiple taxes often leads to high inflation for everyday goods.

18.english_meaning: The minimum proportion of total deposits that commercial banks must hold as reserves with the central bank.
18.hindi_meaning: नकद आरक्षित अनुपात - वाणिज्यिक बैंकों द्वारा अपनी कुल जमा राशि का वह निश्चित हिस्सा जो केंद्रीय बैंक (RBI) के पास सुरक्षित रखना अनिवार्य होता है।
18.example: The central bank increased the Cash Reserve Ratio to control the money supply in the economy.

18.english_meaning: A worker who is hired on a daily or periodic contract basis for farm or non-farm work in exchange for wages.
18.hindi_meaning: आकस्मिक मजदूरी श्रमिक - ऐसा मजदूर जो दैनिक या सामयिक अनुबंध के आधार पर दूसरों के खेतों या उद्यमों में काम करता है और मजदूरी प्राप्त करता है।
18.example: Many rural workers find employment as casual wage labourers during the harvesting season.

18.english_meaning: The policy or practice of acquiring full or partial political control over another country, occupying it with settlers, and exploiting it economically.
18.hindi_meaning: उपनिवेशवाद - किसी शक्तिशाली देश द्वारा दूसरे क्षेत्रों पर अधिकार कर वहां के राजनीतिक और आर्थिक जीवन पर नियंत्रण स्थापित करना और उसका शोषण करना।
18.example: India's economy suffered greatly under British colonialism.

18.english_meaning: Production of crops primarily for sale in the market rather than for family self-consumption.
18.hindi_meaning: कृषि का व्यवसायीकरण - परिवार की खपत के लिए नहीं, बल्कि बाजार में बेचने के लिए फसलों का उत्पादन करना।
18.example: The British promoted the commercialisation of agriculture to secure raw materials for their industries.

18.english_meaning: Former large collective agricultural and administrative units in rural China that integrated governmental, political, and economic functions.
18.hindi_meaning: कम्यून - चीन के ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में स्थापित बड़े सामूहिक संगठन, जिनके पास प्रशासनिक, राजनीतिक और आर्थिक अधिकार होते थे।
18.example: People's communes in China were later replaced by township systems.

18.english_meaning: A representative group of goods and services commonly consumed by a household, used to measure living standards or inflation.
18.hindi_meaning: उपभोग टोकरी - एक परिवार द्वारा उपभोग की जाने वाली वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का समूह, जिसका उपयोग आर्थिक पैटर्न और मुद्रास्फीति को मापने के लिए किया जाता है।
18.example: Cereals and pulses are essential items included in the consumer consumption basket.

18.english_meaning: The action or fact of treating someone unfairly in order to benefit from their work or resources.
18.hindi_meaning: शोषण - किसी व्यक्ति, संसाधन या देश का अपने लाभ के लिए अनुचित या स्वार्थी उपयोग करना।
18.example: Economic exploitation was a primary feature of foreign rule in historical colonies.

18.english_meaning: Relating to factors whose effect on population growth or mortality varies with the population density.
18.hindi_meaning: घनत्व-निर्भर - ऐसे कारक जिनका प्रभाव किसी जनसंख्या के घनत्व के अनुसार घटता या बढ़ता है।
18.example: Food shortage and disease are classic examples of density-dependent population regulators.

18.english_meaning: Too large or too small in comparison to something else; lacking proper proportion.
18.hindi_meaning: अनुपातहीन - किसी अन्य वस्तु की तुलना में आवश्यकता से अधिक या बहुत कम होना।
18.example: A small tax hike resulted in a disproportionate increase in market prices.

18.english_meaning: Relating to the running of a business, organization, or government department.
18.hindi_meaning: प्रशासनिक - किसी संस्था, संगठन या सरकार के प्रबंधन और संचालन से संबंधित।
18.example: The communes handled various administrative and economic duties in rural areas.

19.english_meaning: Failure to make repayment of the principal and interest on a debt on the scheduled date.
19.hindi_meaning: ऋण या मूलधन और ब्याज का समय पर भुगतान करने में विफलता
19.example: The country faced severe economic crisis after it went into default on its international loans.

19.english_meaning: A financial situation where the government's expenditure exceeds its revenue.
19.hindi_meaning: घाटे की वित्तव्यवस्था (ऐसी स्थिति जहाँ सरकार का खर्च उसकी आय से अधिक हो)
19.example: Developing nations often resort to deficit financing to fund infrastructural projects.

19.english_meaning: A concept describing the typical pattern of falling death and birth rates linked with economic development.
19.hindi_meaning: जनसांख्यिकीय संक्रमण (आर्थिक विकास के साथ जन्म और मृत्यु दर में बदलाव का प्रतिरूप)
19.example: India is currently undergoing demographic transition as health standards improve.

19.english_meaning: Allowing wider enterprises to produce goods and services previously restricted to specific groups, such as small-scale industries.
19.hindi_meaning: आरक्षण समाप्त करना (विशेष उद्योगों के लिए आरक्षित वस्तुओं का उत्पादन दूसरों के लिए खोलना)
19.example: The policy of dereservation allowed large firms to manufacture items earlier reserved for small sectors.

19.english_meaning: An official reduction in the value of a country's currency relative to other foreign currencies.
19.hindi_meaning: अमूल्यन (अन्य मुद्राओं की तुलना में अपनी मुद्रा के मूल्य में आधिकारिक कमी)
19.example: Devaluation of the domestic currency can make exports more competitive in the global market.

19.english_meaning: The deliberate sale of a part of government or company capital stock to raise resources and restructure management.
19.hindi_meaning: विनिवेश (संसाधन जुटाने और प्रबंधन बदलने के लिए कंपनी या सरकार की पूंजी का हिस्सा बेचना)
19.example: The government announced its disinvestment plan for several public sector undertakings.

19.english_meaning: Self-employed workers who run their enterprises largely by hiring external labourers.
19.hindi_meaning: नियोक्ता (वे लोग जो कामगारों को काम पर रखकर अपने उद्यम चलाते हैं)
19.example: Local employers gathered to discuss wage policies and labour regulations.

19.english_meaning: An undertaking owned and operated to produce or distribute goods and services mainly for sale.
19.hindi_meaning: उद्यम (वस्तुओं और सेवाओं के उत्पादन या वितरण के लिए स्थापित व्यवसाय)
19.example: Starting a small manufacturing enterprise requires careful financial planning.

19.english_meaning: Shares in the paid-up capital of a company whose holders are considered owners with voting rights.
19.hindi_meaning: समता अंश / शेयर (कंपनी की पूंजी में हिस्सेदारी जो धारक को स्वामित्व और मताधिकार देती है)
19.example: Investors trade equities on the stock exchange to earn dividends and capital gains.

19.english_meaning: An enterprise that employs at least one hired worker for a major part of its operating period in a year.
19.hindi_meaning: प्रतिष्ठान (वह उद्यम जिसमें वर्ष के अधिकांश समय कम से कम एक कामगार नियुक्त हो)
19.example: The factory is registered as a formal commercial establishment under the labour laws.

19.english_meaning: The process of working together to the same end or for mutual benefit.
19.example: Regional cooperation is essential for the economic stability of the continent.

19.english_meaning: Income that a government or company receives regularly.
19.example: Tax collection is the primary source of revenue for the central government.

20.english_meaning: Taxes imposed on goods that are sent out or exported from a country.
20.hindi_meaning: निर्यात शुल्क (वह कर जो देश से बाहर भेजी जाने वाली वस्तुओं पर लगाया जाता है)
20.example: The government levied high export duties on raw materials to encourage domestic manufacturing.

20.english_meaning: Government measures and policies designed to boost the export of goods to achieve higher economic growth.
20.hindi_meaning: निर्यात संवर्धन (निर्यात को बढ़ाने के लिए सरकार द्वारा उठाए गए कदम और उपाय)
20.example: Export promotion schemes help domestic businesses expand into international markets.

20.english_meaning: Family members who work on a family farm or business without receiving cash or kind wages.
20.hindi_meaning: पारिवारिक श्रम (परिवार के सदस्यों द्वारा बिना किसी नकद या वस्तु के रूप में मजदूरी के किया जाने वाला काम)
20.example: Many small farms in rural areas heavily depend on family labour during the harvest season.

20.english_meaning: Establishments that handle the mobilization and allocation of savings, such as commercial and developmental banks.
20.hindi_meaning: वित्तीय संस्थान (ऐसी संस्थाएं जो बचत जुटाने और उनका आवंटन करने का काम करती हैं)
20.example: Financial institutions play a crucial role in providing credit to upcoming entrepreneurs.

20.english_meaning: The use of government taxation and public expenditure to regulate and control economic activities.
20.hindi_meaning: राजकोषीय प्रबंधन (आर्थिक गतिविधियों को नियंत्रित करने के लिए कराधान और सरकारी खर्च का उपयोग)
20.example: Effective fiscal management is essential to control inflation and maintain economic stability.

20.english_meaning: A government's planned actions regarding public finance, revenue mobilization, and expenditure.
20.hindi_meaning: राजकोषीय नीति (देश के वित्तीय संसाधनों को जुटाने और खर्च करने से जुड़ी सरकार की योजनाबद्ध नीतियां)
20.example: The finance minister announced a new fiscal policy aimed at boosting infrastructure development.

20.english_meaning: Long-term investment of foreign assets into domestic structures, equipment, and organizations.
20.hindi_meaning: प्रत्यक्ष विदेशी निवेश / एफ.डी.आई. (घरेलू कंपनियों, संपत्तियों या उपकरणों में विदेशी पूंजी का दीर्घकालिक निवेश)
20.example: Foreign direct investment brings advanced technology and creates new jobs in the host country.

20.english_meaning: The currency or bonds of another country held for international trade and transactions.

42.english_meaning: The process of developing or being developed, leading to growth, advancement, or economic progress.
42.example: Inclusive development is essential for the progress of the nation.

42.english_meaning: A detailed proposal for doing or achieving something, structured over a specific period.
42.hindi_meaning: योजना (किसी कार्य को पूरा करने की रूपरेखा)
42.example: India adopted five-year plans to direct its economic development.

42.english_meaning: A person who is learning a subject or skill, especially a student.
42.example: Learners should critically evaluate historical economic policies.

43.english_meaning: The events that will necessarily happen to a particular person or thing in the future.
43.example: Finally we were masters of our own destiny after years of British rule.

43.english_meaning: A system of production, resource allocation, and distribution of goods and services within a society.
43.example: The leaders of independent India had to decide the type of economic system most suitable for our nation.

43.english_meaning: A political and economic theory of social organization which advocates that the means of production, distribution, and exchange should be owned or regulated by the community as a whole.
43.example: Socialism appealed to Jawaharlal Nehru the most among the different economic systems.

43.english_meaning: The non-human facilities and resources for producing goods, such as factories, land, and raw materials.
43.example: In the former Soviet Union, all the means of production were owned by the government.

43.english_meaning: An economic and political system in which a country's trade and industry are controlled by private owners for profit, rather than by the state.
43.example: Nehru sought an alternative to the extreme versions of capitalism and socialism.

43.english_meaning: The part of an economy that is controlled by the government.
43.example: India would be a socialist society with a strong public sector and private property.

43.english_meaning: A thing aimed at or sought; a goal.
43.example: The central objective of planning in India is to initiate a process of development.

43.english_meaning: To cause a process or action to begin.
43.example: Planning helps to initiate a process of development across the country.

43.english_meaning: Widespread in a particular area or at a particular time.
43.example: Prepare a chart on the different types of economic systems prevalent in the world.

43.english_meaning: The action of spending funds or an amount of money spent.
43.example: Plan a class trip considering the money expenditure involved.

43.english_meaning: To produce something by assembling information collected from various sources.
43.example: Compile these specific goals with the help of your teacher.

43.english_meaning: The health, happiness, and fortunes of a person or group.
43.example: The economic system was chosen to promote the welfare of all rather than a few.

44.english_meaning: An economic system in which trade, industry, and the means of production are controlled by private owners for profit, rather than by the state.
44.hindi_meaning: पूंجیवाद (ऐसी आर्थिक प्रणाली जिसमें उत्पादन के साधन निजी हाथों में होते हैं और उद्देश्य लाभ कमाना होता है)
44.example: In a market economy or capitalism, goods are produced based on consumer demand and profitability.

44.english_meaning: Operating on the principles of capitalism; favoring private enterprise and market forces.
44.example: In a capitalist society, goods are distributed on the basis of purchasing power.

44.english_meaning: Relating to socialism; advocating that the means of production, distribution, and exchange should be owned or regulated by the community as a whole.
44.example: A socialist society decides what goods are to be produced in accordance with the needs of society.

44.english_meaning: An economic system in which production and prices are determined by unrestricted competition between privately owned businesses.
44.example: In a market economy, decisions regarding production and distribution depend on market forces of supply and demand.

44.english_meaning: The financial ability of individuals or households to buy goods and services.
44.hindi_meaning: क्रय शक्ति (वस्तुओं और सेवाओं को खरीदने की वित्तीय क्षमता)
44.example: Distribution under capitalism is based on purchasing power rather than human needs.

44.english_meaning: Needing a large workforce or a great deal of human effort to produce goods or services.
44.example: If labour is cheaper than capital, more labour-intensive methods of production will be used.

44.english_meaning: An economic system combining private and public enterprise, utilizing both market forces and government intervention.
44.example: Most economies in the world today are mixed economies where both the government and the market play active roles.

44.english_meaning: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold, or any useful thing.
44.example: Low-cost housing for the poor will not be produced as a commercial commodity if demand is not backed by purchasing power.

44.english_meaning: The action of sharing something out among a number of recipients, or the way in which wealth and goods are divided in a society.
44.example: How goods and services should be distributed among people is a fundamental question for every economic system.

44.english_meaning: Relating to or running within the home country or internal market.
44.example: Goods can be sold profitably either in the domestic market or in foreign markets.

44.english_meaning: A fundamental truth or proposition that serves as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior.
44.example: In principle, distribution under socialism is supposed to be based on what people need.

44.english_meaning: A person who purchases goods and services for personal use.
44.example: In a market economy, only those consumer goods will be produced that are in demand.

45.english_meaning: The state of a country or region in terms of the production and consumption of goods and services and the supply of money.
45.example: The government is taking steps to strengthen the Indian economy.

45.english_meaning: Guidelines or principles given in the Indian Constitution for framing laws and policies by the government.
45.example: The Directive Principles of the Indian Constitution guide the social and economic policy of the country.

45.english_meaning: A former agency of the government of India established in 1950 to oversee the country's economic and social development through five-year plans.
45.example: The Planning Commission was set up with the Prime Minister as its Chairperson.

45.english_meaning: The adoption of new technology, ideas, and social practices to improve efficiency and output.
45.example: Modernisation of agriculture helps in increasing overall productivity.

45.english_meaning: Reliance on one's own capabilities, resources, and judgment without depending on others.
45.example: Achieving self-reliance in food grain production was a major goal for independent India.

45.english_meaning: The quality of being fair and impartial; ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reach every section of the society.
45.example: Economic planning must ensure equity so that wealth is distributed fairly.

45.english_meaning: To be in conflict with so as to make the truth or validity of something doubtful.
45.example: The policies of the plan should not contradict the core goals of development.

45.english_meaning: The amount of something produced by a person, machine, or industry.
45.example: Growth refers to an increase in the country's capacity to produce the output of goods and services.

45.english_meaning: Wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organization or contributed for a purpose such as starting a company or investing.
45.example: Larger stock of productive capital is essential for industrial growth.

45.english_meaning: A long-term plan spanning over a longer duration, such as twenty years, providing a broad framework for short-term plans.
45.example: The five-year plans were supposed to provide the basis for the perspective plan.

45.english_meaning: The supply of water to land or crops to help growth, typically by means of channels.
45.example: Power generation and irrigation are key sectors where the state plays a commanding role.

45.english_meaning: Having a position of authority or control, or occupying a dominant position in a specific sector.
45.example: The government plays a commanding role in infrastructure development like power generation.

46.english_meaning: The action of creating or preparing something methodically, such as a plan or policy.
46.hindi_meaning: निर्माण या रचना (किसी योजना या नीति को तैयार करने की प्रक्रिया)
46.example: The formulation of the five-year plans required careful economic analysis.

46.english_meaning: An expert in or practitioner of statistics.
46.example: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis was a world-renowned statistician.

46.english_meaning: An event, discovery, or change marking an important stage or turning point in history or a field.
46.hindi_meaning: ऐतिहासिक या मील का पत्थर (एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ या उपलब्धि)
46.example: The Second Five Year Plan was a landmark contribution to Indian economic development.

46.english_meaning: A person who designs, makes, or brings about something.
46.hindi_meaning: रचनाकार या सूत्रधार (किसी व्यवस्था या योजना को गढ़ने वाला)
46.example: Mahalanobis is regarded as the architect of Indian planning.

46.english_meaning: Inspiring respect and admiration; having high status.
46.example: He was elected as a fellow of Britain's Royal Society, a prestigious scientific organization.

46.english_meaning: An organization founded for a specific educational, scientific, or research purpose.
46.hindi_meaning: संस्थान (विशेष उद्देश्य के लिए स्थापित संगठन)
46.example: He established the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta.

46.english_meaning: A meeting or medium where ideas and views on a particular issue can be exchanged.
46.example: His journal served as a respected forum for statisticians to discuss their ideas.

46.english_meaning: Successful, authoritative, and commanding great respect.
46.example: He invited many distinguished economists from around the world to advise on planning.

46.english_meaning: To establish or recognize the characteristics or worth of someone or something.
46.example: Mahalanobis had a unique ability to identify talented individuals early in their careers.

46.english_meaning: Expressing adverse or disapproving comments or judgments.
46.example: Some invited economists were very critical of the socialist principles of the second plan.

46.english_meaning: A specialist in a particular branch of study, especially the humanities.
46.example: Being willing to listen to critics is the mark of a true scholar.

46.english_meaning: Advocating or practicing socialism, focusing on public or state ownership of resources.
46.example: The economic framework of the second plan was largely based on socialist principles.

47.english_meaning: The total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a specific year.
47.hindi_meaning: सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (एक वर्ष में देश में उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल बाजार मूल्य)
47.example: An increase in the Gross Domestic Product indicates economic growth.

47.english_meaning: The contribution made by different sectors (agriculture, industry, and services) to the economy.
47.hindi_meaning: संरचनात्मक गठन (अर्थव्यवस्था में विभिन्न क्षेत्रों जैसे कृषि, उद्योग और सेवा का योगदान)
47.example: The structural composition of India shifted significantly over the decades.

47.english_meaning: The adoption of new technology and changes in social outlook, such as gender equality.
47.hindi_meaning: आधुनिकीकरण (नई तकनीक को अपनाना और सामाजिक दृष्टिकोण में बदलाव, जैसे समानता)
47.example: Modernisation in agriculture involves using high-yielding seed varieties.

47.english_meaning: Promoting economic growth and development by using a nation's own resources rather than depending on imports.
47.hindi_meaning: आत्मनिर्भरता (विदेशी आयातों पर निर्भर रहने के बजाय अपने संसाधनों का उपयोग करना)
47.example: The early five-year plans placed great emphasis on national self-reliance.

47.english_meaning: The branch of an economy concerned with farming, cultivation, and animal husbandry.
47.hindi_meaning: कृषि क्षेत्र (खेती और पशुपालन से जुड़ा अर्थव्यवस्था का हिस्सा)
47.example: Historically, the agricultural sector employed a major share of India's workforce.

47.english_meaning: The sector of an economy that involves manufacturing, production of goods, and factories.
47.hindi_meaning: औद्योगिक क्षेत्र (विनिर्माण, कारखानों और वस्तुओं के उत्पादन से जुड़ा क्षेत्र)
47.example: Development policies often aim to expand the industrial sector to create jobs.

47.english_meaning: The sector of the economy that produces intangible services rather than physical goods, such as banking and education.
47.hindi_meaning: सेवा क्षेत्र (बैंकिंग, शिक्षा और परिवहन जैसी सेवाएं प्रदान करने वाला क्षेत्र)
47.example: By 1990, the service sector grew to form a large part of India's GDP.

47.english_meaning: Successful in material terms; flourishing financially and socially.
47.example: A society that utilizes the talents of all its citizens tends to be more prosperous.

47.english_meaning: A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen, especially one whose cause is in question.
47.example: The rapid growth of the service sector was an unusual economic phenomenon.

47.english_meaning: Happened or caused to happen at a faster rate.
47.example: Economic reforms accelerated the pace of industrial development.

47.english_meaning: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
47.hindi_meaning: वैश्वीकरण (देश की अर्थव्यवस्था को दुनिया की अर्थव्यवस्था के साथ जोड़ना)
47.example: The onset of globalisation in 1991 transformed the Indian market.

47.english_meaning: A person's point of view or general attitude towards life and society.
47.example: Education helps in bringing positive changes to the social outlook.

48.english_meaning: Reliance on one's own powers and resources rather than those of others; avoiding foreign dependence.
48.example: Achieving self-reliance in food grain production was a primary goal for independent India.

48.english_meaning: The authority of a state to govern itself or another state; supreme power or independence.
48.example: The leaders feared that foreign dependence might make India's sovereignty vulnerable.

48.english_meaning: Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.
48.example: Heavy reliance on foreign imports can leave a country vulnerable to external pressures.

48.english_meaning: The quality of being fair and impartial; fairness in the distribution of wealth and opportunities.
48.example: Economic planning must ensure equity so that the benefits of growth reach the poor.

48.english_meaning: The state of being successful, especially in financial terms; good fortune and wealth.
48.example: The government aimed to share the fruits of national prosperity with every citizen.

48.english_meaning: Difference in size, degree, circumstances, etc.; lack of equality, especially in wealth or status.
48.example: Reducing inequality in the distribution of wealth is essential for a welfare state.

48.english_meaning: To succeed in getting something, typically after a lot of effort.
48.example: India set specific goals to attain rapid economic development through five-year plans.

48.english_meaning: Persons who act as a link between people in order to try and bring about an agreement or deal, such as middlemen in land systems.
48.example: Land reforms were introduced to remove intermediaries between the government and actual tillers.

48.english_meaning: Described or marked by certain features or qualities.
48.example: The colonial agricultural sector was characterised by stagnation and backwardness.

48.english_meaning: A forcible overthrow of a government or social order, or a dramatic and wide-reaching change in conditions.
48.example: The introduction of HYV seeds ushered in a green revolution in Indian agriculture.

48.english_meaning: Showed or guided someone somewhere, or marked the beginning of something new.
48.example: New agricultural policies ushered in an era of higher food grain production.

48.english_meaning: Connected with or belonging to a country that controls another country.
48.example: India inherited a stagnant economy due to two centuries of colonial rule.

49.english_meaning: Landlords or intermediaries under the British system who collected rent from cultivators.
49.hindi_meaning: ज़मींदार (मध्यस्थ जो किसानों से मालगुज़ार या लगान वसूलते थे)
49.example: The abolition of zamindars freed tenants from exploitation.

49.english_meaning: The state or quality of producing something, especially crops or goods, at a high rate.
49.example: The low productivity of the agricultural sector forced India to import food.

49.english_meaning: Fairness and justice in the distribution of wealth and resources.
49.example: Land ceiling was introduced to promote equity in the agricultural sector.

49.english_meaning: Changes in the ownership and laws regarding landholdings to benefit cultivators.
49.example: Land reforms primarily refer to changes in the ownership of landholdings.

49.english_meaning: Middlemen or agents who act as a link between two parties, such as landlords and government.
49.example: Steps were taken to abolish intermediaries and make tillers the owners of land.

49.english_meaning: Things that motivate or encourage someone to do something or work harder.
49.example: Ownership of land gives incentives to tillers to invest in improvements.

49.english_meaning: Fixing the maximum limit of land that an individual can legally own.
49.example: Land ceiling helps to reduce the concentration of land ownership in a few hands.

49.english_meaning: The clustering or gathering of power, wealth, or ownership in very few places or people.
49.hindi_meaning: संकेंद्रण (कुछ ही हाथों में सीमित होना)
49.example: The purpose of land ceiling was to reduce the concentration of land ownership.

49.english_meaning: People who occupy land or property rented from a landlord.
49.example: Thousands of tenants came into direct contact with the government.

49.english_meaning: Treated unfairly in order to benefit from one's work or labor.
49.example: The tenants were freed from being exploited by the zamindars.

49.english_meaning: Granted or bestowed an honor, right, or property upon someone.
49.example: The ownership conferred on tenants gave them the incentive to increase output.

49.english_meaning: People who prepare land and grow crops; farmers.
49.example: Cultivators will take more interest if they own the land.

50.english_meaning: A law or a set of laws made by a government.
50.hindi_meaning: कानून या विधायिका द्वारा पारित अधिनियम
50.example: The government introduced new legislation to protect the rights of tenant farmers.

50.english_meaning: People who rent and farm land or live in a house owned by someone else.
50.hindi_meaning: बटाईदार या किराएदार जो दूसरों की भूमि पर खेती करते हैं
50.example: Many tenants were unlawfully evicted from the land by wealthy landowners.

50.english_meaning: Expelled or forced to leave a property, house, or land legally.
50.hindi_meaning: कानूनी रूप से बेदखल करना या निकालना
50.example: Poor farmers were wrongfully evicted from their ancestral farming lands.

50.english_meaning: Tenant farmers who give a share of their crops as rent to the landowners.
50.hindi_meaning: बटाईदार जो फसल का एक हिस्सा लगान के रूप में देते हैं
50.example: Land reforms failed to provide adequate financial relief to landless agricultural labourers and sharecroppers.

50.english_meaning: Fixing the maximum limit of land that an individual or family can own.
50.hindi_meaning: भूमि की अधिकतम सीमा तय करने का कानून
50.example: The land ceiling legislation faced severe hurdles and delays in the courts.

50.english_meaning: Obstacles, difficulties, or problems that must be overcome.
50.example: Big landlords created legal hurdles to delay the implementation of land reforms.

50.english_meaning: Made use of unfairly in order to gain an advantage or loop-holes.
50.hindi_meaning: गलत फायदा उठाना या शोषण करना
50.example: Landowners exploited loopholes in the laws to retain large estates.

50.english_meaning: A state of inactivity, lack of growth, or standing still.
50.hindi_meaning: ठहराव या विकास की गति का रुक जाना
50.example: The long period of stagnation in Indian agriculture ended with the Green Revolution.

50.english_meaning: The basic physical and organizational structures needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.
50.hindi_meaning: बुनियादी ढांचा (जैसे सिंचाई, बिजली, सड़कें आदि)
50.example: Lack of proper agricultural infrastructure kept crop productivity extremely low.

50.english_meaning: The supply of water to land or crops to help growth, typically by means of channels.
50.hindi_meaning: सिंचाई (फसलों को कृत्रिम रूप से पानी देना)
50.example: Reliable irrigation facilities are essential for cultivating high-yielding crop varieties.

50.english_meaning: Wealthy, prosperous, or having a great deal of money.
50.example: In the initial phase, the benefits of HYV seeds were restricted to more affluent states like Punjab.

50.english_meaning: The quality or condition of being able to provide everything one needs without external help.
50.example: The Green Revolution enabled India to achieve self-sufficiency in food grain production.

51.english_meaning: The portion of agricultural produce which is sold in the market by the farmers after keeping what is needed for self-consumption.
51.hindi_meaning: विपणित आधिक्य (कृषि उपज का वह हिस्सा जो किसान अपनी खपत के बाद बाजार में बेचते हैं)
51.example: A large marketed surplus of food grains helped lower their market prices.

51.english_meaning: Of considerable importance, size, or worth; large in amount.
51.example: A substantial amount of agricultural produce was sold in the market.

51.english_meaning: A large increase in crop production in developing countries achieved by the use of fertilizers, pesticides, and high-yielding crop varieties.
51.hindi_meaning: हरित क्रांति (कृषि उत्पादन में भारी वृद्धि लाने वाली तकनीक व नीति)
51.example: The green revolution made the nation self-sufficient in food grain production.

51.english_meaning: To become smaller, fewer, or lower; decrease.
51.example: The price of food grains declined relative to other items of consumption.

51.english_meaning: To obtain or get something, especially with care or effort.
51.hindi_meaning: प्राप्त करना, खरीदना (विशेषकर सरकारी स्तर पर)
51.example: The government managed to procure a sufficient amount of food grains for buffer stocks.

51.hindi_meaning: अत्यधिक रूप से, भारी मात्रा में
51.example: The nation had immensely benefited from the introduction of new agricultural technologies.

51.english_meaning: Great differences, inequalities, or imbalances between people or groups.
51.example: The new policy risked increasing economic disparities between small and big farmers.

51.english_meaning: To have enough money or resources to buy or do something.
51.hindi_meaning: वहन करने की क्षमता होना, सामर्थ्य होना
51.example: Only the big farmers could afford the expensive required inputs for HYV seeds.

51.english_meaning: To harvest a crop or to receive a reward or benefit as a consequence of an action.
51.example: Big farmers were reaping most of the benefits of the green revolution.

51.english_meaning: Likely or liable to suffer from or experience something unpleasant.
51.hindi_meaning: प्रवृत्त, प्रवण या संवेदनशील (शिकार होने की संभावना)
51.example: HYV crops were more prone to attack by pests.

51.english_meaning: A destructive insect or other animal that attacks crops, food, livestock, etc.
51.hindi_meaning: कीट, फसल को नुकसान पहुँचाने वाले जीव
51.example: A sudden pest attack destroyed the entire crop in the field.

51.english_meaning: The using up of a resource, or the purchase and use of goods and services by consumers.
51.example: Low-income groups spend a large percentage of their income on food consumption.

52.english_meaning: Supported with money from the government or an organization so that the price is lower.
52.example: The government provided subsidised fertilisers to help small farmers.

52.english_meaning: Resources such as money, effort, or materials used in production or farming.
52.hindi_meaning: कृषि आगत / उत्पादन संसाधन (जैसे बीज, उर्वरक)
52.example: Farmers need financial support to buy essential agricultural inputs.

52.english_meaning: A large-scale increase in agricultural production in developing countries achieved through the use of high-yielding varieties of seeds, pesticides, and fertilizers.
52.example: The green revolution made India self-sufficient in food grain production.

52.english_meaning: A good reason or explanation for something.
52.example: Economists are debating the economic justification of agricultural subsidies.

52.english_meaning: Something that encourages a person to do something or work harder.
52.example: Subsidies provided an incentive for farmers to adopt new technology.

52.english_meaning: The action or fact of choosing to take up, follow, or use something.
52.example: The successful adoption of modern techniques improved crop yields.

52.english_meaning: To stop using or supplying something gradually over a period of time.
52.example: Some experts believe that subsidies should be phased out eventually.
Farmers in the more prosperous regions benefited greatly from the policy.

52.english_meaning: Completely removing or getting rid of something.
52.example: Eliminating subsidies might increase financial hardships for poor farmers.

52.english_meaning: Difference in size, degree, circumstances, etc.; lack of equality.
52.example: Policies should be designed to reduce economic inequality in society.

52.english_meaning: The quality of being fair and impartial.
52.example: Government policies must uphold the goal of social and economic equity.

52.english_meaning: The state or quality of producing something, especially crops or goods, efficiently.
52.example: Agricultural productivity increased significantly by the late 1960s.

53.english_meaning: Bringing wealth and success; flourishing financially.
53.hindi_meaning: समृद्ध, खुशहाल या आर्थिक रूप से सफल
53.example: As a nation becomes more prosperous, the contribution of agriculture to its GDP usually declines.

53.english_meaning: To a notably large extent or degree; significantly.
53.hindi_meaning: काफी हद तक या महत्वपूर्ण रूप से
53.example: The proportion of GDP contributed by agriculture declined considerably between 1950 and 1990.

53.english_meaning: To take in or incorporate something, such as workforce or resources, into a larger system.
53.hindi_meaning: आत्मसात करना या (श्रमशक्ति आदि को) अपने अंदर समाहित करना
53.example: The industrial and service sectors failed to absorb the surplus workers from the agricultural sector.

53.english_meaning: To protect (something, especially an environmental resource) from harm or destruction.

53.example: When electricity and water are provided at a subsidised rate, they tend to be used wastefully.

53.english_meaning: To use up the supply or resources of something drastically.
53.hindi_meaning: रिक्त करना या (संसाधनों को) तेजी से घटाना
53.example: Growing water-intensive crops in dry regions will further deplete the scarce underground water resources.

54.english_meaning: In a way that is easily perceived or understood; clearly.

54.english_meaning: Wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organization or contributed for a purpose such as starting a company.

54.english_meaning: Experts in economics who study the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.

54.english_meaning: Strive to gain or win something by defeating or establishing superiority over others.
54.example: Do you think our farmers will be able to compete with heavily subsidized farmers from developed countries?

55.english_meaning: Former; previous; belonging to an earlier time.

55.english_meaning: Relating to a system of society where the means of production and distribution are controlled by the public/state.

55.english_meaning: To add something to improve or complete it.
55.example: The private sector could supplement the efforts of the public sector.

55.english_meaning: A reduction in price or a special advantage granted by the government.
55.example: Backward industrial units were given concessions such as tax benefits.

55.english_meaning: A tax or rate charged by a government or utility provider, such as for electricity.
55.example: Industries in backward regions were provided electricity at a lower tariff.

55.english_meaning: Enlarging or varying the range of products or fields of operation.
55.hindi_meaning: विविधता लाना, उत्पादों का विस्तार करना
55.example: Existing industries needed a license for diversifying production into new goods.

55.english_meaning: Combining in such a way as to enhance or emphasize each other's qualities.

55.english_meaning: Relating to or characteristic of a particular region or district.

56.english_meaning: A principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

56.hindi_meaning: आयात प्रतिस्थापन (विदेशी वस्तुओं की जगह घरेलू उत्पादन को बढ़ावा देना)

56.english_meaning: A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports.
56.example: Tariffs make imported goods more expensive and discourage their use.

56.english_meaning: A limited or fixed number or amount of people or things, in this case, imports, allowed.

56.english_meaning: A conception of or belief about something.

56.english_meaning: A sign or piece of information that shows something exists or is happening.

56.english_meaning: Encompassing a variety of different types of products or activities.

57.example: The public sector played a major role in the industrial development of India.

57.english_meaning: Industries in which manufacturing, production, and rendering of services are done on a small scale.
57.hindi_meaning: लघु उद्योग (कम पूंजी और छोटे पैमाने पर चलने वाले उद्योग)
57.example: The government encouraged small-scale industries to create more employment opportunities.

57.english_meaning: Wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organization or contributed for a purpose such as starting a company.
57.hindi_meaning: पूंजी (व्यापार शुरू करने के लिए लगाया गया धन)

57.hindi_meaning: स्वदेशी (देश में ही उत्पन्न या निर्मित)
57.example: Protection from foreign competition helped in the growth of indigenous industries.

57.english_meaning: A business or company, especially a commercial venture.
57.example: Some economists are critical of the performance of many public sector enterprises.

57.english_meaning: Exclusive possession or control of the supply of or trade in a commodity or service.
57.hindi_meaning: एकाधिकार स्थापित करना (किसी वस्तु या सेवा पर पूर्ण नियंत्रण रखना)

57.english_meaning: The action of providing or supplying something for use.
57.hindi_meaning: प्रावधान या आपूर्ति (किसी सेवा या वस्तु को उपलब्ध कराना)

58.english_meaning: Transferred from private ownership to state or government ownership.

58.english_meaning: An official permit or authorization to start or conduct a business activity.

59.hindi_meaning: परिणत होना; किसी परिणाम या निष्कर्ष पर पहुँचना

59.english_meaning: The process of adapting something to modern needs or habits, often through new technology.

62.example: Liberalisation opened the domestic market to global competition.

62.english_meaning: The transfer of a business, industry, or service from public to private ownership or control.
62.example: Privatisation of state-owned enterprises aimed to improve operational efficiency.

62.english_meaning: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
62.example: Globalisation has connected markets across different continents.

62.english_meaning: The process of developing or being developed, leading to growth, advancement, or maturity.
62.example: Infrastructure development is vital for national economic progress.

62.english_meaning: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
62.example: The country adopted a new strategy to overcome the balance of payments crisis.

62.english_meaning: An area or arena in which commercial dealings are conducted, governed by the forces of supply and demand.
62.example: Market forces dictate the prices of goods in a capitalist economy.

63.english_meaning: The process of growing, changing, or advancing to a more advanced state.
63.example: The government focused on planned development to improve the country's infrastructure.

63.english_meaning: The total capacity of a country's manufacturing and industrial enterprises.
63.example: India successfully built a strong industrial base over forty years of planned efforts.

63.english_meaning: Needing no outside help in satisfying one's basic needs.
63.example: With increased crop yields, the nation became self-sufficient in the production of food grains.

63.english_meaning: A part or section of something larger.
63.example: A major segment of the rural population depends on farming for survival.

63.english_meaning: Means of securing the necessities of life, such as income or employment.
63.example: Millions of families rely on agriculture as their primary source of livelihood.

63.english_meaning: The difference in total value between payments into and out of a country over a period.
63.example: A severe crisis in the balance of payments forced India to rethink its economic policies.

63.english_meaning: The bringing of something new into use or operation for the first time.
63.example: The introduction of new technology improved efficiency in the factory.

63.english_meaning: Policy changes aimed at improving economic performance, often involving liberalization.
63.example: The economic reforms of 1991 opened up the Indian market to global trade.

63.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone, evaluation or judgment.
63.example: This chapter provides a detailed appraisal of the reform process.

63.english_meaning: A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end.
63.example: Industrialization is a long and continuous process of economic growth.

63.english_meaning: The effects or consequences that are likely to result from an action or decision.
63.example: The committee analyzed the social implications of the new tax policy.

63.english_meaning: A time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger.
63.example: The country faced a major financial crisis before taking corrective measures.

64.english_meaning: The improvement or amendment of what is wrong, corrupt, or unsatisfactory.
64.example: Economic reforms were introduced in India in the year 1991.

64.english_meaning: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by an organization or government.
64.example: The government announced a new industrial policy to boost growth.

64.english_meaning: To grasp mentally; to understand fully.
64.example: Students must comprehend the long-term effects of economic changes.

64.english_meaning: A system of parts working together in a machine or a process by which something is achieved.
64.example: We need to understand the mechanism through which these policies were implemented.

64.english_meaning: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
64.example: Globalisation has opened up new markets for Indian goods and services.

64.english_meaning: The effect or consequence that an action or decision will have.
64.example: We studied the social and economic implications of the new trade agreement.

64.english_meaning: The removal or reduction of government regulations in a specific field, usually to encourage economic activity.
64.example: Liberalisation allowed private companies to enter sectors previously reserved for the public sector.

64.english_meaning: The transfer of a business, industry, or service from public to private ownership or control.
64.example: Privatisation of certain state-run enterprises aims to improve efficiency.

64.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone; an expert evaluation or estimation.
64.example: The chapter provides a critical appraisal of India's economic reforms.

64.english_meaning: An area or portion of an economy, society, or sphere of activity.
64.example: The agricultural, industrial, and service sectors form the backbone of the economy.

64.english_meaning: The circumstances, conditions, or relevant historical facts preceding an event.
64.example: It is important to study the historical background before analyzing current policies.

64.english_meaning: A marked effect or influence that something has on a situation or person.
64.example: The reform process had a major impact on employment and income levels.

65.english_meaning: The removal or reduction of government rules and restrictions on the private business and trade sectors.
65.hindi_meaning: उदारीकरण (व्यापार और उद्योगों पर से सरकारी नियंत्रण और प्रतिबंधों को कम करना या हटाना)
65.example: Liberalisation of the economy in 1991 opened the doors for foreign investment in India.

65.english_meaning: The transfer of ownership, property, or business from the government to the private sector.
65.hindi_meaning: निजीकरण (सरकारी स्वामित्व वाले उद्यमों या संपत्तियों को निजी हाथों में सौंपना)
65.example: The government considered privatisation of loss-making public sector enterprises to improve efficiency.

65.english_meaning: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
65.hindi_meaning: वैश्वीकरण (विभिन्न देशों की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं और संस्कृतियों का वैश्विक स्तर पर एकीकरण)
65.example: Globalisation has made a wide variety of international goods available in the local markets.

65.english_meaning: An economic system combining private enterprise and a state monopoly.
65.hindi_meaning: मिश्रित अर्थव्यवस्था (ऐसी अर्थव्यवस्था जिसमें पूंजीवादी और समाजवादी दोनों प्रणालियों के गुण शामिल हों)
65.example: Since independence, India chose to follow a mixed economy framework.

65.english_meaning: Hindering or impeding the progress or smooth movement of something.
65.hindi_meaning: बाधा डालना या रोकना (प्रगति या कार्य में रुकावट पैदा करना)
65.example: Excessive rules and regulations ended up hampering the process of economic growth.

65.english_meaning: A state of inactivity, lack of growth, or failure to develop.
65.hindi_meaning: ठहराव (विकास या गतिविधि की गति का रुक जाना)
65.example: India started its developmental path from a state of near economic stagnation.

65.english_meaning: Showing a great deal of variety; very different from one another.
65.hindi_meaning: विविधकृत (जिसमें कई तरह की विविधता या भिन्नता हो)
65.example: India has successfully developed a diversified industrial sector producing various goods.

65.english_meaning: Money or other assets held by a central bank or other monetary authority that can be used to pay for its international obligations.
65.hindi_meaning: विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार (अंतरराष्ट्रीय भुगतान के लिए केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा रखी गई विदेशी मुद्रा की राशि)
65.example: The country's foreign exchange reserves dropped so low that they were insufficient for even a fortnight.

65.english_meaning: Made worse, more intense, or more severe.
65.hindi_meaning: और अधिक गंभीर होना या बढ़ जाना (समस्या का और जटिल होना)
65.example: The economic crisis was further compounded by the rapidly rising prices of essential goods.

65.english_meaning: The amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.
65.example: When government expenditure exceeds income, it borrows funds to finance the fiscal deficit.

65.english_meaning: Go past or beyond a target, limit, or expected level.
65.hindi_meaning: निर्धारित सीमा से आगे निकल जाना या अधिक खर्च कर देना
65.example: The government had to overshoot its revenue limits to meet crucial developmental challenges like poverty.

65.english_meaning: A general agreement among a group of people.
65.example: There is a broad consensus in the world today that economic development alone is not enough.

66.english_meaning: Income that a government or company receives regularly.
66.hindi_meaning: राजस्व (सरकार या कंपनी को प्राप्त होने वाली आय)
66.example: The government's revenue from taxes was not enough to cover all its expenses.

66.english_meaning: Government-owned corporations or companies in India.
66.example: Public sector undertakings play a major role in the country's industrial development.

66.english_meaning: Money in foreign currencies held by a central bank to pay for imports and debts.
66.hindi_meaning: विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार (विदेशी मुद्रा का वह भंडार जो केंद्रीय बैंक के पास होता है)
66.example: India faced a severe crisis when its foreign exchange reserves dropped to a very low level.

66.english_meaning: Recklessly extravagant or wasteful in the use of resources.
66.hindi_meaning: अपव्ययी (धन या संसाधनों का अत्यधिक और लापरवाही से खर्च करने वाला)
66.example: The country suffered economically due to profligate spending by the administration.

66.english_meaning: Not able to be maintained at the current rate or level.
66.hindi_meaning: अस्यनीय / जिसे लंबे समय तक न चलाया जा सके
66.example: Borrowing money continuously to run the government became completely unsustainable.

66.english_meaning: A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.
66.example: The government introduced stabilization measures to bring inflation under control.

66.english_meaning: To remove or loosen restrictions on economic activity and trade.
66.hindi_meaning: उदार बनाना (व्यापार या अर्थव्यवस्था पर से प्रतिबंध हटाना)
66.example: International agencies expected India to liberalise its economy by removing restrictions.

66.english_meaning: Conditions attached to the provision of a loan or financial assistance.
66.hindi_meaning: शर्तें (जो किसी ऋण या सहायता के साथ जोड़ी जाती हैं)
66.example: India had to agree to several conditionalities imposed by the World Bank and IMF.

66.english_meaning: The main point, emphasis, or direction of an argument, policy, or plan.
66.example: The main thrust of the new policy was to create a competitive economic environment.

66.english_meaning: Short-term measures intended to correct economic weaknesses and control inflation.
66.hindi_meaning: स्थिरीकरण (अर्थव्यवस्था में अल्पकालिक सुधार के उपाय)
66.example: Stabilisation measures were urgently needed to fix the balance of payments.

66.english_meaning: Relating to the arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of a complex system.
66.hindi_meaning: संरचनात्मक (किसी व्यवस्था के ढाँचे से संबंधित)
66.example: Structural reforms aim to improve the long-term efficiency of the economy.

66.english_meaning: Inflexibility or stiffness that prevents proper functioning or adaptation.
66.hindi_meaning: कठोरता या अनम्यूपन (बाधाएँ जो विकास रोकती हैं)
66.example: The government removed various economic rigidities to boost international competitiveness.

67.english_meaning: The removal of government controls and restrictions on economic activities to encourage private participation and growth.
67.hindi_meaning: उदारीकरण (आर्थिक गतिविधियों पर से सरकारी नियंत्रण और प्रतिबंधों को हटाना)
67.example: Liberalisation in 1991 opened various sectors of the Indian economy to private enterprises.

67.english_meaning: The transfer of ownership, property, or business from the government to the private sector.
67.hindi_meaning: निजीकरण (सरकार से निजी क्षेत्र को स्वामित्व या कारोबार का हस्तांतरण)
67.example: Privatisation often aims to improve efficiency and management in industrial enterprises.

67.english_meaning: The integration of a country's economy with the world economy through trade, investment, and technology.
67.hindi_meaning: वैश्वीकरण (व्यापार और निवेश के माध्यम से किसी देश की अर्थव्यवस्था का विश्व अर्थव्यवस्था के साथ एकीकरण)
67.example: Globalisation allows companies to trade goods and services seamlessly across international borders.

67.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone, or estimating the value, nature, or quality of a policy or situation.
67.hindi_meaning: मूल्यांकन या समीक्षा (किसी नीति या स्थिति के गुण-दोष का आकलन)
67.example: This chapter provides a detailed appraisal of the economic reforms introduced in 1991.

67.english_meaning: Factors that provide resistance, delay, or obstruction to something, making progress difficult.
67.example: Excessive rules and laws became major hindrances in the country's economic growth.

67.english_meaning: The reduction or elimination of government power in a particular industry, usually enacted to create more competition.
67.example: Deregulation of the industrial sector removed the need for mandatory government licenses in most categories.

67.english_meaning: A person who sets up a business or businesses, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.
67.hindi_meaning: उद्यमी (नया व्यवसाय शुरू करने वाला व्यक्ति)
67.example: Earlier, every entrepreneur had to obtain government permission before starting a firm.

67.english_meaning: Full of risk; dangerous, especially to health or safety.
67.example: Manufacture of hazardous chemicals still requires strict government licensing and regulation.

67.english_meaning: Companies and industries involved in the research, development, and distribution of medicinal drugs.
67.example: Pharmaceuticals remain one of the few product categories that still require industrial licensing.

67.english_meaning: Freed from exclusive reservation, allowing general production rather than restricting it to a specific sector.
67.hindi_meaning: आरक्षित श्रेणी से मुक्त किए गए (उत्पाद)
67.example: Many items previously produced exclusively by small-scale industries have now been dereserved.

67.english_meaning: An official or agency appointed to supervise a particular industry or business activity and enforce rules.
67.hindi_meaning: नियामक (नियम तय करने और निगरानी रखने वाली संस्था)
67.example: The role of the Reserve Bank of India shifted from a strict regulator to a financial sector facilitator.

67.english_meaning: A person or organization that makes an action, process, or institution easier and smoother.
67.example: Economic reforms transformed the central bank into a facilitator of the financial market.

68.english_meaning: To reorganize a business or system in a way that makes it more efficient and effective.
68.hindi_meaning: व्यवस्थित करना या अधिक तर्कसंगत और प्रभावी बनाना
68.example: The bank decided to rationalise its branch network to reduce operational costs.

68.english_meaning: Large investment funds and institutions from outside a country that invest in its financial markets.
68.hindi_meaning: विदेशी संस्थागत निवेशक (जैसे म्यूचुअल फंड या पेंशन फंड जो किसी अन्य देश के बाजारों में निवेश करते हैं)
68.example: Foreign Institutional Investors are now allowed to invest freely in Indian financial markets.

68.english_meaning: A government's policy regarding taxation and public expenditure.
68.hindi_meaning: राजकोषीय नीति (सरकार की कराधान और सार्वजनिक खर्च से संबंधित नीति)
68.example: Tax reforms are a core component of the government's fiscal policy.

68.english_meaning: The illegal practice of not paying taxes, or paying less than what is legally owed.
68.hindi_meaning: कर की चोरी (कानून से छिपकर कर न चुकाना)
68.example: High income tax rates in the past were considered a major reason for tax evasion.

68.english_meaning: A tax imposed on the profits of business enterprises and companies.
68.hindi_meaning: निगम कर (कंपनियों के मुनाफे पर लगने वाला कर)
68.example: The rate of corporation tax has been gradually reduced to encourage business growth.

68.english_meaning: Imposed or collected (as a tax, fee, or fine).
68.hindi_meaning: आरोपित करना या लगाना (जैसे कर या शुल्क)
68.example: Indirect taxes are levied on the sale of goods and services.

68.english_meaning: The act of obeying rules, laws, or regulations.
68.hindi_meaning: अनुपालन (नियमों या कानूनों का पालन करना)
68.example: Tax procedures were simplified to encourage better compliance among taxpayers.

68.english_meaning: Reduced the official value of a country's currency in relation to foreign currencies.
68.hindi_meaning: अवमूल्यन करना (विदेशी मुद्राओं के मुकाबले अपने देश की मुद्रा का मूल्य घटाना)
68.example: In 1991, the rupee was devalued to resolve the balance of payments crisis.

68.english_meaning: A statement of all transactions made between entities in one country and the rest of the world over a defined period.
68.hindi_meaning: भुगतान संतुलन (किसी देश के सभी आर्थिक लेन-देन का हिसाब)
68.example: The devaluation of the rupee was an immediate measure to resolve the balance of payments crisis.

68.english_meaning: The removal or reduction of government controls or restrictions on a private industry.
68.hindi_meaning: उदारीकरण (सरकारी नियंत्रणों और पाबंदियों में ढील देना)
68.example: Liberalisation of the trade regime aimed to increase international competitiveness.

68.english_meaning: The ability of a business, country, or product to compete successfully with others.
68.hindi_meaning: प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता (प्रतियोगिता में टिके रहने या सफल होने की क्षमता)
68.example: Trade reforms helped boost the international competitiveness of Indian industries.

68.english_meaning: To protect someone or something from harm or damage.
68.example: Certain managerial powers were retained with the RBI to safeguard account-holders.

69.english_meaning: The removal or reduction of government rules and restrictions on private businesses and trade.
69.hindi_meaning: उदारीकरण (व्यापार और उद्योगों पर से सरकारी नियंत्रण या प्रतिबंधों को कम करना)
69.example: Liberalisation of the economy invited major foreign investments into the country.

69.english_meaning: The transfer of a business, industry, or service from public (government) to private ownership or control.
69.hindi_meaning: निजीकरण (सरकारी स्वामित्व वाले उद्यमों को निजी हाथों में सौंपना)
69.example: Privatisation aims to improve the efficiency and productivity of loss-making public sector undertakings.

69.english_meaning: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
69.hindi_meaning: वैश्वीकरण (देश की अर्थव्यवस्था को विश्व अर्थव्यवस्था के साथ जोड़ना)
69.example: Globalisation has made consumer goods from across the world easily available in local markets.

69.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone, or an expert evaluation.
69.hindi_meaning: मूल्यांकन (किसी चीज़ के गुण, मूल्य या स्थिति का आकलन करना)
69.example: The chapter provides an appraisal of the economic reforms introduced in 1991.

69.english_meaning: Owned and operated by the national government.
69.hindi_meaning: राष्ट्रीयकृत (सरकार के स्वामित्व और नियंत्रण के अधीन)
69.example: Major commercial banks in India were nationalised to extend banking services to rural areas.

69.english_meaning: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality.
69.example: The government imposed strict quantitative limits on the import of certain electronic items.

69.english_meaning: A limiting condition or measure, especially a legal one.
69.example: The removal of trade restrictions helped boost exports significantly.

69.english_meaning: Taxes or duties to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports.
69.hindi_meaning: आयात शुल्क / कर (विदेशों से आने वाले सामान पर लगने वाला कर)
69.example: High tariffs were levied on foreign goods to protect domestic industries from competition.

69.english_meaning: Taking apart or gradually ending a system, organization, or structure.
69.hindi_meaning: समाप्त करना / हटाना (किसी व्यवस्था या ढांचे को धीरे-धीरे खत्म करना)
69.example: The trade policy focused on the dismantling of licensing procedures for imports.

69.english_meaning: Formally put an end to a system, practice, or institution.
69.hindi_meaning: समाप्त कर दिया गया / रद्द कर दिया गया
69.example: Import licensing was completely abolished except for hazardous industries.

69.english_meaning: Risky; dangerous, especially to health or safety.
69.example: Strict regulations are applied to hazardous chemical manufacturing units to protect the environment.

69.english_meaning: As good as or better than others of a comparable nature.
69.example: Export duties were removed to make Indian products more competitive in global markets.

70.english_meaning: The transfer of a business, industry, or service from public to private ownership or control.
70.hindi_meaning: निजीकरण (सरकारी स्वामित्व वाले उद्यम को निजी हाथों में सौंपना)
70.example: Privatisation of government-owned companies aims to improve their overall efficiency and financial discipline.

70.english_meaning: The action of an organization or government selling or liquidating its asset or subsidiary, specifically selling part of the equity of public sector enterprises to the public.
70.hindi_meaning: विनिवेश (सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उद्यमों की हिस्सेदारी या इक्विटी जनता को बेचना)
70.example: The government raised funds through the disinvestment of shares in public sector enterprises.

70.english_meaning: A business or company, especially a large or government-owned one.
70.example: Public sector enterprises play a crucial role in providing basic infrastructure to the nation.

70.english_meaning: The value of the shares issued by a company.
70.hindi_meaning: इक्विटी / शेयर पूंजी (कंपनी के शेयरों का मूल्य या स्वामित्व हिस्सा)
70.example: The government decided to sell a portion of its equity in profit-making PSUs.

70.english_meaning: A controlled behavior or a system of rules regulating conduct, especially financial management.
70.example: One of the key goals of economic reforms was to instill financial discipline in public enterprises.

70.english_meaning: The process of adapting something to modern needs or habits, often through new technology and methods.
70.hindi_meaning: आधुनिकरण (नई तकनीकों और तरीकों को अपनाना)
70.example: The reforms were introduced to facilitate the modernisation of industrial production.

70.english_meaning: Contemplated or predicted as a possible or desirable future event.
70.hindi_meaning: परिकल्पित (भविष्य के लिए अनुमानित या योजनाबद्ध करना)
70.example: It was envisaged that private capital would enhance the efficiency of state-run companies.

70.english_meaning: Relating to management or the job of a manager.
70.example: Improved managerial capabilities helped the company reduce operational costs.

70.english_meaning: The right or condition of self-government, freedom to make decisions independently.
70.example: Navratna companies were granted greater financial and operational autonomy.

70.english_meaning: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.
70.example: Public sector companies were established primarily to build the core infrastructure of the country.

70.english_meaning: A person with an interest or concern in something, especially a business.
70.hindi_meaning: हितधारक (वे लोग जिनका किसी व्यवसाय या संस्था में हित या सरोकार हो)
70.example: Public enterprises are expected to remain accountable to all their stakeholders.

70.english_meaning: To claim that someone has done something illegal or wrong, typically without proof.
70.example: Some scholars allege that the government is selling off national assets too cheaply.

71.english_meaning: The removal or reduction of government regulations, controls, and restrictions in an economy.

78.hindi_meaning: आलोचक (जो किसी नीति या विचार के विरोधी हों या कमियां बताते हों)
78.example: Critics argue that the new trade policy will harm domestic industries.

78.english_meaning: To accept standards that are lower than is desirable, or to bring into danger or disrepute.

78.english_meaning: Great differences, especially in economic status, opportunities, or treatment.

78.english_meaning: The unfair situation in which some people have more rights, better opportunities, or more money than other people.
