78.english_meaning: To make a problem, injury, or offense worse or more serious.
78.hindi_meaning: और अधिक गंभीर बनाना / बिगाड़ देना
78.example: Lack of rain aggravated the drought situation in the region.

78.english_meaning: Existing in one particular place or area in large numbers or amounts rather than being spread out.
78.hindi_meaning: केंद्रित (किसी एक स्थान या क्षेत्र तक सीमित)
78.example: Industrial growth was largely concentrated in a few major cities.

78.english_meaning: Means of securing the necessities of life, such as income or employment.
78.example: Agriculture provides livelihoods for millions of people in rural India.

78.english_meaning: A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money over time.
78.example: High inflation makes it difficult for middle-class families to save money.

78.english_meaning: The removal of government controls and restrictions in a particular area, usually to encourage economic development.
78.hindi_meaning: उदारीकरण (सरकारी नियंत्रणों और प्रतिबंधों में ढील देना)
78.example: Economic liberalisation in 1991 transformed the Indian industrial landscape.

78.english_meaning: The action of an organization or government selling or liquidating its assets or subsidiary investments, typically public sector undertakings.
78.hindi_meaning: विनिवेश (सरकारी उद्यमों में अपनी हिस्सेदारी बेचना)
78.example: The government planned disinvestment in several loss-making public enterprises.

78.english_meaning: The action or process of combining two or more things or organizations so that they work together effectively.
78.example: Global integration has boosted international trade and cooperation.

79.english_meaning: The removal or reduction of government rules and restrictions on economic activity and trade.
79.hindi_meaning: उदारीकरण (आर्थिक गतिविधियों पर सरकारी नियंत्रण या प्रतिबंधों को हटाना या कम करना)
79.example: Liberalisation in 1991 opened the Indian economy to private enterprises and foreign investment.

79.english_meaning: The transfer of a business, industry, or service from public (government) ownership to private ownership.
79.hindi_meaning: निजीकरण (सरकारी स्वामित्व वाले उद्यमों का प्रबंधन या स्वामित्व निजी हाथों में सौंपना)
79.example: The government announced the privatisation of several loss-making public sector undertakings.

79.english_meaning: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
79.hindi_meaning: वैश्वीकरण (देश की अर्थव्यवस्था को विश्व अर्थव्यवस्था के साथ जोड़ना)
79.example: Globalisation has increased international trade and cultural exchange across the world.

79.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone to determine their value, quality, or success.
79.hindi_meaning: मूल्यांकन या समीक्षा (किसी वस्तु या प्रक्रिया के महत्व या प्रदर्शन का आकलन)
79.example: The chapter provides a critical appraisal of economic reforms introduced in India.

79.english_meaning: The official reduction of the value of a country's currency within a fixed exchange rate system.
79.hindi_meaning: अवमूल्यन (अन्य मुद्राओं की तुलना में देश की मुद्रा के आधिकारिक मूल्य को कम करना)
79.example: The devaluation of the rupee made Indian exports more competitive in the international market.

79.english_meaning: A person or organization that makes an action, process, or institution easier or more efficient.
79.hindi_meaning: सुगमकर्ता (किसी प्रक्रिया या कार्य को आसान बनाने वाला)
79.example: The central bank changed its role from a rigid controller to a financial sector facilitator.

79.english_meaning: Formed or involving two sides, countries, or parties, especially mutually.
79.hindi_meaning: द्विपक्षीय (दो देशों या पक्षों के बीच होने वाला)
79.example: India signed a bilateral trade agreement with its neighboring country to boost commerce.

79.english_meaning: A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports.
79.hindi_meaning: प्रशुल्क या आयात कर (आयातित वस्तुओं पर लगाया जाने वाला कर)
79.example: High tariffs were imposed on foreign goods to protect domestic industries from competition.

79.english_meaning: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality.
79.hindi_meaning: मात्रात्मक (गुणवत्ता के बजाय मात्रा या संख्या से संबंधित)
79.example: Quantitative restrictions limit the exact physical amount of goods that can be imported.

79.english_meaning: Obtaining goods or services from an outside or foreign supplier, especially in place of an internal source.
79.hindi_meaning: आउटसॉर्सिंग (कंपनी के काम को बाहरी या विदेशी एजेंसी को सौंपना)
79.example: India has become a major global destination for IT and customer service outsourcing.

79.english_meaning: A group of top-performing public sector undertakings in India given financial autonomy by the government.
79.hindi_meaning: नवरत्न (बेहतर प्रदर्शन करने वाले प्रमुख सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उद्यम)
79.example: The government granted special managerial autonomy to selected public enterprises under the navaratna policy.

79.english_meaning: In a way that prevents success or development; harmfully or unfavorably.
79.hindi_meaning: प्रतिकूल रूप से (नकारात्मक या हानिकारक रूप से)
79.example: The agricultural sector appeared to be adversely affected by the new economic reforms.

80.english_meaning: Relating to the economics or economy of a country, region, or society.
80.example: The country experienced a significant economic growth rate last year.

80.english_meaning: The speed at which a variable, such as GDP, increases over a specific period.
80.example: The GDP growth rate indicates the overall health of the economy.

80.english_meaning: The manner or style in which information or data is shown to an audience.
80.example: The techniques of presentation of data help in understanding statistics easily.

80.english_meaning: The practice or science of collecting and analyzing numerical data in large quantities.
80.example: You study various methods of data collection in your statistics course.

80.english_meaning: To explain the meaning of information, words, or actions.
80.example: Students were asked to interpret the line graph based on the given table.

80.english_meaning: An organized body of people with a particular purpose, such as a business or government department.
80.example: Both public and private organisations supply electricity in different states.

80.english_meaning: An area of land under the jurisdiction of a ruler or state.
80.example: Union territories are governed directly by the central government in India.

80.english_meaning: The state or fact of living or existing together at the same time or in the same place.
80.example: The dual system highlights the co-existence of public and private sectors.

80.english_meaning: The advantages or good qualities of something.
80.example: We should discuss both the merits and demerits of a mixed economy.
Every economic policy has its own merits and demerits.

80.english_meaning: Operating in or spanning multiple countries.
80.example: Many multinational companies expanded their businesses into developing markets.

80.english_meaning: The fact or state of being independent, free from outside control.
80.example: India's industrial landscape changed significantly after independence.

81.english_meaning: The removal of government controls and restrictions in a country's economy.
81.hindi_meaning: उदारीकरण (सरकारी नियंत्रणों और प्रतिबंधों को हटाना)
81.example: Liberalisation of the economy in 1991 opened the doors for private and foreign investments.

81.english_meaning: The transfer of a business, industry, or service from public (government) to private ownership or control.
81.hindi_meaning: निजीकरण (सरकारी स्वामित्व से निजी हाथों में संपत्ति या व्यवसाय का हस्तांतरण)
81.example: Privatisation helps in improving efficiency and competitive spirit in public sector enterprises.

81.english_meaning: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
81.hindi_meaning: वैश्वीकरण (राष्ट्रीय अर्थव्यवस्था का विश्व अर्थव्यवस्था के साथ एकीकरण)
81.example: Globalisation has made a wide variety of foreign goods available in the Indian domestic market.

81.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone, or a formal evaluation.
81.hindi_meaning: मूल्यांकन (किसी स्थिति या कार्य का जायजा लेना)
81.example: The textbook chapter provides a detailed appraisal of the economic reforms introduced in 1991.

81.english_meaning: A course of action intended to influence or control the behaviour of a country's economy.
81.hindi_meaning: आर्थिक नीति (देश की अर्थव्यवस्था को नियंत्रित करने के लिए सरकार की नीतियां)
81.example: The New Economic Policy aimed to pull India out of its severe balance of payments crisis.

81.english_meaning: Makes an action or process easy or easier.
81.example: The World Trade Organization facilitates international trade among different member nations.

81.english_meaning: The improvement or amendment of what is wrong, corrupt, or unsatisfactory.
81.example: Economic reforms are necessary for the sustainable growth of a developing nation.
India introduced structural reforms at the behest of international financial institutions.

81.english_meaning: Available as another possibility or choice.
81.example: The government had no alternative left due to the depleting foreign exchange reserves.

81.english_meaning: A time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger.
81.example: The balance of payments crisis in 1991 forced India to mortgage its gold reserves.

81.english_meaning: The use of a source of information in order to ascertain something or cite authorities.
81.hindi_meaning: संदर्भ (प्रयुक्त पुस्तकों या स्रोतों की सूची)
81.example: Students should check the references at the end of the chapter for further reading.

81.english_meaning: An underlying basis or principle, or an organization funded for a purpose.
81.example: Academic Foundation is a well-known publishing house that prints books on Indian economy.

82.english_meaning: The process of developing or being developed, especially economically or socially.
82.example: Economic development is crucial for improving the living standards of citizens.

82.english_meaning: The process of making plans for something, especially economic or administrative strategies.
82.example: Effective economic planning helps in the optimal allocation of national resources.

82.english_meaning: The removal of government controls or restrictions in a country's economy.
82.example: Economic liberalisation opened the Indian market to foreign investments in 1991.

82.english_meaning: Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level without depleting natural resources.
82.example: The country aims to achieve sustainable growth without harming the environment.

82.english_meaning: Relating to government revenue, taxes, and public spending.
82.example: Fiscal policies are designed by the government to manage the economy.

82.english_meaning: Changes and improvements brought about in a system, law, or organization.
82.example: Structural economic reforms transformed the industrial sector in India.

82.english_meaning: The state of a country or region in terms of the production and consumption of goods and services.
82.example: The Indian economy witnessed rapid growth after the introduction of new policies.

82.english_meaning: A time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger, particularly in financial markets.
82.example: India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991.

82.english_meaning: The action of making a problem or suffering less severe.
82.example: Poverty alleviation programs are essential for social justice.

82.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone, such as evaluating a government plan.
82.example: The appraisal document of the plan highlights the achievements of the past years.

82.english_meaning: The practice or science of collecting and analyzing numerical data in large quantities.
82.example: The Reserve Bank publishes comprehensive statistics on the Indian economy.

82.english_meaning: An official group of people entrusted with a particular task or administrative duty.
82.example: The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating five-year plans in India.

83.english_meaning: Happening or existing at the present time.
83.example: The teacher discussed the current economic situation of the country.

83.english_meaning: Tasks or situations that test someone's abilities or present difficulties.
83.example: Poverty and unemployment are major challenges for development.

83.english_meaning: Dealing with or confronting a difficult situation or problem.
83.example: Many industries are facing a shortage of skilled labor.

83.english_meaning: The state of a country or region in terms of the production and consumption of goods and services.
83.example: Agriculture forms the backbone of the rural Indian economy.

83.english_meaning: An individual thing or person regarded as separate and distinct, or a section of a book.
83.example: This textbook is divided into several units for easy learning.

83.english_meaning: To print a book or article again.
83.example: The NCERT textbook was released in a new reprint edition.

83.english_meaning: Relating to India or its people, culture, or economy.
83.example: Indian agriculture has seen significant modernization over the decades.

83.english_meaning: Relating to the economics or society of a country.
83.example: The government launched new policies to boost economic growth.

83.english_meaning: The process of developing or being developed, especially economically.
83.example: Sustainable development ensures progress without harming the environment.

83.english_meaning: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government or party.
83.example: Fiscal policy is crucial for controlling inflation in the market.

83.english_meaning: An increase in the amount, value, or importance of something.
83.example: Rapid industrial growth helps create new jobs for youth.

83.english_meaning: An area or portion of an economy, such as agriculture, industry, or services.
83.example: The tertiary sector contributes heavily to India's GDP today.

84.english_meaning: People who are acquiring new knowledge or skills.
84.example: The textbook is designed to help learners understand complex economic concepts.
Students must grasp the basic concepts before moving on to advanced topics.

84.english_meaning: A stock or supply of money, staff, materials, or other assets that can be drawn on.
84.example: Water is a vital natural resource for human survival.

84.english_meaning: Wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organization or contributed for a purpose.
84.example: Investing in machinery and technology increases physical capital.

84.english_meaning: The action of forming or process of being formed.
84.example: Capital formation is essential for the economic development of a country.

84.english_meaning: The process of developing or being developed, often leading to growth and advancement.
84.example: Human development focuses on improving the well-being of people.

84.english_meaning: The action or process of investing money for profit or material result.
84.example: Investment in education yields high returns in the long run.

84.english_meaning: Relating to economics or the economy, especially regarding financial matters.
84.example: Rapid economic growth helps reduce poverty in developing nations.

84.english_meaning: The process of increasing in amount, value, or proportion.
84.example: Economic growth is measured by the increase in a country's total output.

84.english_meaning: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.
84.example: The government allocates funds for public healthcare and schooling.

84.english_meaning: The action or fact of achieving a goal or status.
84.example: Higher educational attainment leads to better employment opportunities.

84.english_meaning: Providing education or relating to the field of education.

85.example: Investment in education and health helps in building strong human capital.

85.english_meaning: The gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form.
85.hindi_meaning: विकास / क्रमिक उत्थान - किसी चीज़ का धीरे-धीरे सरल से अधिक जटिल रूप में विकसित होना।
85.example: The evolution of mankind has been driven by the ability to transmit knowledge.

85.english_meaning: To pass on or spread information, knowledge, or ideas to others.
85.hindi_meaning: आगे पहुंचाना / संचित ज्ञान को संचारित करना।
85.example: Older generations transmit their wisdom and skills to the younger generation.

85.english_meaning: In a way that achieves maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense.
85.hindi_meaning: कुशलतापूर्वक - बिना किसी बर्बादी के बेहतरीन तरीके से कार्य करना।
85.example: Proper training enables workers to complete their tasks more efficiently.

85.hindi_meaning: परिणामस्वरूप / अतः - किसी कारण के प्रभाववश।
85.example: She worked very hard for the exam and, consequently, scored the highest marks.

85.english_meaning: To grant or bestow a benefit, quality, or advantage upon someone.
85.hindi_meaning: प्रदान करना / देना - किसी को कोई अधिकार या लाभ देना।
85.example: Higher education often confers greater career opportunities and social respect.

85.english_meaning: The creation of better or more effective products, processes, technologies, or ideas.
85.hindi_meaning: नवाचार / नई खोज - नए विचार, तकनीक या उत्पाद विकसित करना।
85.example: Science and technology education stimulates continuous innovations in society.

85.english_meaning: To make an action, process, or objective easier or more likely to happen.
85.hindi_meaning: सुगम बनाना / आसान करना - किसी प्रक्रिया को सरल बनाना।
85.example: Digital technology facilitates online learning for students everywhere.

85.english_meaning: The action or process of adapting or being adapted to new conditions or environments.
85.hindi_meaning: अनुकूलन - नई परिस्थितियों या वातावरण के अनुसार खुद को ढालना।
85.example: The adaptation of new farming techniques helps increase agricultural output.

85.english_meaning: Spending or using up time, money, or energy resources.
85.hindi_meaning: खर्च करना / व्यय करना - धन, समय या ऊर्जा लगाना।
85.example: Expending resources on public health is essential for national development.

85.english_meaning: The state or quality of being productive; the effectiveness of productive effort, especially in industry.
85.hindi_meaning: उत्पादकता - कार्य करने या वस्तुएं पैदा करने की क्षमता और मात्रा।
85.example: Using modern tools and machinery significantly increases farm productivity.

85.english_meaning: Existing but not yet developed or manifest; hidden or concealed abilities.
85.hindi_meaning: गुप्त / अंतर्निहित - छिपी हुई क्षमताएं जो अभी प्रकट नहीं हुईं हैं।
85.example: Good education helps children discover and bring out their latent talents.

86.english_meaning: Experts who study the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.
86.example: Economists have stressed the need for expanding educational opportunities in the country.

86.english_meaning: Happens or makes something happen faster or earlier.
86.example: Proper planning accelerates the development process of a nation.

86.english_meaning: Man-made goods such as tools, machinery, and factories used in production.
86.example: A country can turn physical resources like land into physical capital like factories.

86.english_meaning: The stock of knowledge, habits, social and personality attributes, and creativity embodied in the ability to perform labor so as to produce economic value.
86.example: Investment in education and health helps in building strong human capital.

86.english_meaning: Having the necessary ability, knowledge, or skill to do something successfully.
86.example: Societies need sufficient human capital in the form of competent professionals.

86.english_meaning: The action or process of investing money for profit or material result.
86.example: We need investment in human capital to produce more skilled workers.

86.english_meaning: The action of creatively forming or producing something.
86.example: The formation of human capital is linked to a country's economic growth.

86.english_meaning: Movement of people from one place to another, often in search of better jobs or education.
86.example: Investments in education, health, on-the-job training, and migration contribute to human capital formation.

86.english_meaning: Forced or obliged to do something.
86.example: A sick labourer without medical facilities is compelled to abstain from work.

86.english_meaning: To restrain oneself from doing or enjoying something.
86.hindi_meaning: दूर रहना / अलग रहना (कार्य से विरत रहना)
86.example: Illness forces workers to abstain from their daily duties.

86.english_meaning: The state or quality of being productive; effectiveness of productive effort.
86.example: Poor health leads to a significant loss of productivity in the workforce.

86.english_meaning: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

87.english_meaning: Medical measures taken to prevent diseases rather than curing them once they occur, such as vaccinations.
87.hindi_meaning: निवारक औषधि (बीमारियों को रोकने के लिए किए जाने वाले उपाय, जैसे टीकाकरण)
87.example: Vaccination is an essential part of preventive medicine.

87.english_meaning: Medical treatment and intervention provided during an illness to cure or heal the patient.
87.hindi_meaning: उपचारात्मक औषधि (बीमारी के दौरान इलाज और चिकित्सा हस्तक्षेप)
87.example: Curative medicine is required when a person falls seriously ill.

87.english_meaning: Conditions relating to public health, especially the provision of clean drinking water and adequate sewage disposal.
87.hindi_meaning: स्वच्छता (जनस्वास्थ्य से जुड़ी व्यवस्था, जैसे साफ पेयजल और मल-मूत्र का निकास)
87.example: Good sanitation is necessary to prevent the spread of waterborne diseases.

87.english_meaning: The process of adding to the stock of human capital, such as investments in education, health, and training.
87.hindi_meaning: मानव पूंजी निर्माण (शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य और प्रशिक्षण में निवेश द्वारा मानव कौशल व क्षमता में वृद्धि)
87.example: Health and education expenditures are major sources of human capital formation.

87.english_meaning: Practical training provided to employees within a firm to enhance their skills and productivity.
87.hindi_meaning: कार्यस्थल पर प्रशिक्षण (कर्मचारियों की उत्पादकता और कौशल बढ़ाने के लिए फर्म द्वारा दिया जाने वाला प्रशिक्षण)
87.example: The company provides on-the-job training for all new technical recruits.

87.english_meaning: The effectiveness of productive effort, measured in terms of the rate of output per unit of input.
87.hindi_meaning: उत्पादकता (संसाधनों के उपयोग से वस्तुओं और सेवाओं के उत्पादन की क्षमता)
87.example: Proper training leads to enhanced worker productivity.

87.english_meaning: To move from one region or country to another, typically for work or better living conditions.

87.example: Many rural workers migrate to cities in search of better employment opportunities.

87.english_meaning: Mental or emotional stress and non-monetary difficulties experienced when moving to a strange socio-cultural environment.
87.hindi_meaning: मानसिक लागत (नए और अनजान सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक माहौल में रहने से होने वाला मानसिक तनाव व कष्ट)

87.english_meaning: To be heavier, greater, or more significant than something else.
87.hindi_meaning: भारी पड़ना या अधिक महत्वपूर्ण होना

99.english_meaning: The action of spending funds or an amount of money spent.
99.hindi_meaning: व्यय / खर्चा (धन खर्च करने की क्रिया या खर्च की गई राशि)
99.example: Government expenditure on education has increased this year.

99.english_meaning: The action or process of intervening, especially by a government to affect an economy or situation.
99.hindi_meaning: हस्तक्षेप (विशेष रूप से अर्थव्यवस्था या स्थिति को प्रभावित करने के लिए सरकार द्वारा उठाया गया कदम)
99.example: Government intervention in the health sector ensures affordable care for the poor.

99.english_meaning: An increase in the production of goods and services in an economy over a specific period.
99.hindi_meaning: आर्थिक विकास / आर्थिक वृद्धि (एक निश्चित अवधि में वस्तुओं और सेवाओं के उत्पादन में वृद्धि)
99.example: Education plays a vital role in accelerating economic growth.

99.english_meaning: Difference in social status, wealth, or opportunity between people.
99.hindi_meaning: असमानता (लोगों के बीच सामाजिक स्थिति, धन या अवसरों में अंतर)
99.example: Economic policies aim to reduce income inequality in society.

99.english_meaning: Movement of people from one place to another, often for employment or better living conditions.
99.hindi_meaning: प्रवास / पलायन (रोजगार या बेहतर स्थिति के लिए एक स्थान से दूसरे स्थान पर जाना)
99.example: Rural-urban migration often happens in search of better job opportunities.

99.english_meaning: The action of making practical and effective use of something.
99.hindi_meaning: उपयोग / सदुपयोग (किसी वस्तु का व्यावहारिक और प्रभावी उपयोग करना)
99.example: Proper utilisation of human resources leads to national development.

99.english_meaning: To make an action or process easy or easier.
99.hindi_meaning: सुविधा प्रदान करना / आसान बनाना (किसी प्रक्रिया या कार्य को सरल बनाना)
99.example: Digital tools facilitate online learning for students.

99.english_meaning: To encourage or cause activity or development in something.
99.hindi_meaning: प्रोत्साहित करना / गति देना (किसी गतिविधि या विकास को बढ़ावा देना)
99.example: Tax cuts can stimulate economic activity in the market.

99.english_meaning: To buy or obtain an asset, object, or knowledge for oneself.
99.hindi_meaning: प्राप्त करना / हासिल करना (ज्ञान, कौशल या संपत्ति अर्जन करना)

100.english_meaning: To formally join, enroll, or make a list of items or people
100.hindi_meaning: सूचीबद्ध करना या नाम दर्ज करना
100.example: Enlist the various sources that provide information regarding education and health.

100.english_meaning: A government department headed by a minister
100.example: The annual reports of Union Ministries of Education and Health are very informative.

100.english_meaning: A brief statement or account of the main points of something
100.example: Read the annual reports and make summaries of them.

100.english_meaning: An area or portion of an economy or society
100.example: Read the chapter on the social sector in the Economic Survey.

100.english_meaning: Relating to the economy or economics
100.example: The Economic Survey provides valuable data on the country's development.

100.english_meaning: A general view, examination, or description of someone or something
100.example: The Economic Survey outlines the progress of various social policies.

100.english_meaning: The skills, knowledge, and experience possessed by an individual or population, viewed in terms of their value or cost to an organization or country
100.example: Gary S. Becker wrote a foundational book titled 'Human Capital'.

100.english_meaning: The action or state of including or of being included within a group or structure
100.example: The report focuses on India Human Development Report towards social inclusion.

100.english_meaning: The practice or science of collecting and analyzing numerical data in large quantities
100.example: Educational Statistics at a glance is published by the Ministry of Education.

100.english_meaning: The action of spending funds or an amount of money spent
100.example: The study measures the impact of transfers on elementary education expenditure.

100.english_meaning: The action of making things equal or uniform
100.example: Measuring equalisation transfers to Indian States is important for balanced regional growth.

100.english_meaning: A source of information cited in a book or article
100.example: Students should check the references at the end of the chapter for further reading.

101.english_meaning: A process of improving the quality of life and economic well-being of people living in rural areas.
101.hindi_meaning: ग्रामीण विकास - ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में रहने वाले लोगों के जीवन स्तर और आर्थिक कल्याण को बेहतर बनाने की प्रक्रिया।
101.example: Rural development is essential for the overall economic growth of India.

101.hindi_meaning: महत्वपूर्ण / निर्णायक - अत्यंत आवश्यक या महत्वपूर्ण।
101.example: Agriculture plays a crucial role in providing food security to the nation.

101.english_meaning: The ability of a customer to obtain goods or services before payment, based on the trust that payment will be made in the future (loans or financial assistance).
101.hindi_meaning: साख / ऋण - भविष्य में भुगतान करने के भरोसे पर वस्तुएं या धन प्राप्त करने की सुविधा (लोन)।
101.example: Farmers need easy access to agricultural credit to buy seeds and fertilizers.

101.english_meaning: The action or business of promoting and selling products or services, including market research and advertising.
101.hindi_meaning: विपणन / बाजारीकरण - उत्पादों को बेचने और बाजार तक पहुँचाने की प्रक्रिया।
101.example: Effective marketing helps farmers get better prices for their crops.

101.english_meaning: The process of a business or economy expanding its operations into new areas or activities.
101.hindi_meaning: विविधीकरण - किसी अर्थव्यवस्था या व्यवसाय में नए क्षेत्रों या गतिविधियों को शामिल करना।
101.example: Crop diversification reduces the financial risk for farmers.

101.english_meaning: Producing or achieving a large amount or result; capable of making goods or services.
101.hindi_meaning: उत्पादक / उपयोगी - वस्तुओं या सेवाओं का उत्पादन करने में सक्षम।
101.example: Engaging in productive activities during the off-season supplements rural income.

101.english_meaning: To cause to continue for a period of time; to keep alive or support.
101.hindi_meaning: बचाये रखना / बनाए रखना - किसी चीज़ को निरंतर जारी रखना या सहारा देना।
101.example: Small businesses help rural families sustain their livelihoods.

101.english_meaning: Means of securing the necessities of life, such as income and employment.
101.hindi_meaning: आजीविका - जीवनयापन के साधन या कमाने के जरिया।
101.example: Fishing and handicrafts are the primary livelihoods of coastal communities.

101.english_meaning: The quality of being worthy of attention; importance.
101.hindi_meaning: महत्व / तात्पर्य - किसी बात का महत्व या उपयोगिता।
101.example: The teacher explained the significance of water conservation in agriculture.

101.english_meaning: Relating to or derived from living matter; grown or made without the use of artificial chemicals.
101.hindi_meaning: जैविक - प्राकृतिक रूप से उत्पादित, जिसमें कृत्रिम रसायनों का प्रयोग न किया गया हो।
101.example: Organic farming is better for both human health and soil fertility.

101.english_meaning: Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level; avoiding the depletion of natural resources.
101.hindi_meaning: धारणीय / संपोषणीय - प्राकृतिक संसाधनों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
101.example: Sustainable development ensures that future generations have enough resources.

101.english_meaning: Connected with something else; linked or related.
101.hindi_meaning: संबंधित - किसी अन्य चीज़ से जुड़ा हुआ।
101.example: Poverty and unemployment are major problems associated with backward regions.

102.english_meaning: A comprehensive action-oriented process focused on the economic and social development of rural areas lagging behind.
102.example: Rural development is essential for the overall progress of the Indian economy.

102.english_meaning: A means of securing the necessities of life, such as income or employment.
102.example: Agriculture is the major source of livelihood in the rural sector.

102.english_meaning: A state of extremely low living standards and severe deprivation of basic human needs.
102.example: One-fourth of rural India still lives in abject poverty.

102.english_meaning: Complete; including all or nearly all elements or aspects of something.
102.example: Rural development is a comprehensive term covering various economic and social aspects.

102.english_meaning: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.
102.example: Infrastructure development like electricity and irrigation is vital for villages.

102.english_meaning: The action of making a problem or suffering less severe.
102.example: Special measures are required for the alleviation of poverty in rural areas.

102.english_meaning: The effectiveness of productive effort, measured in terms of the rate of output per unit of input.
102.example: Farmers need support to increase the productivity of their land.

102.english_meaning: To enlarge or vary the range of products or fields of activity.
102.example: Rural workers need opportunities to diversify into various non-farm productive activities.

102.english_meaning: The quality of being worthy of attention; importance.
102.example: We should attach great significance to rural development.

102.english_meaning: The action or fact of spreading something, especially information, widely.
102.example: Information dissemination helps farmers adopt modern agricultural research.

102.english_meaning: New plans or processes started to achieve a particular purpose or solve a problem.
102.example: Fresh initiatives are needed for the development of rural India.

102.english_meaning: To strongly suggest the truth or existence of something not expressly stated.
102.example: What does rural development actually imply for the economy?

103.english_meaning: A comprehensive action plan designed to improve the economic and social conditions of people living in rural areas.
103.example: Providing proper healthcare and education is essential for rapid rural development.

103.english_meaning: Mover or caused to move more slowly; reduced in the rate of progress or growth.
103.example: The growth rate of the agriculture sector decelerated significantly after 1991.

103.english_meaning: Liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse.
103.example: In recent years, the agricultural sector has become highly volatile.

103.english_meaning: Lacking the quality or quantity required; insufficient.
103.example: Inadequate infrastructure in rural areas hampers economic growth.

103.english_meaning: The process of a workforce becoming increasingly employed on casual or temporary contracts rather than permanent ones.
103.example: The increasing casualisation of employment has worsened distress in rural areas.

103.english_meaning: To delay or prevent someone or something by obstructing them; hinder.
103.example: Lack of proper roads and electricity can impede rural development.

103.english_meaning: The action of diversifying something or making it more varied, such as engaging in non-farm activities alongside farming.
103.example: Agricultural diversification helps farmers earn a stable income throughout the year.

103.english_meaning: The introduction of a new element or quality, such as money or capital, into something.
103.example: Economic growth in rural areas depends primarily on the timely infusion of capital.

103.english_meaning: The time gap between the initial investment or sowing of crops and the eventual realization of income from production.
103.hindi_meaning: गर्भाधान अवधि / फसल बोने से आय प्राप्त होने के बीच का समय अंतराल
103.example: Farmers need credit because of the long gestation period between crop sowing and harvesting.

103.english_meaning: To make use of meanly or unfairly for one's own advantage.
103.example: Moneylenders often exploited poor farmers by charging exorbitant interest rates.

103.english_meaning: A situation in which a debt is difficult or impossible to repay, typically because high interest payments prevent the principal from being paid down.
103.example: Manipulating accounts kept vulnerable farmers trapped in a permanent debt-trap.

103.english_meaning: Banking practices that prioritize social and environmental impacts, ensuring credit reaches neglected sectors like rural areas.
103.example: India adopted social banking in 1969 to expand rural credit facilities.

104.english_meaning: The practice of using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully, often involving saving.
104.example: The thrift and credit society was started to encourage small savings among poor women.

104.english_meaning: To bring together or collect resources, funds, or people for a particular purpose.
104.example: These societies successfully mobilised Rs 1 crore as thrift savings.

104.english_meaning: The highest or governing organization that coordinates and oversees other institutions in a particular sector.
104.example: NABARD was set up as an apex body to coordinate rural financing.

104.english_meaning: A person or thing that signals or foreshadows the approach of something significant or a major change.
104.example: The Green Revolution was a harbinger of major changes in the agricultural credit system.

104.english_meaning: The process of widening the range of activities, products, or investments.
104.example: The policy led to the diversification of the portfolio of rural credit towards production.

104.english_meaning: The established system of formal organizations and frameworks that govern a sector.
104.example: The institutional structure of rural banking consists of commercial banks, RRBs, and cooperatives.

104.english_meaning: To distribute or provide something, such as money, services, or goods, to a population.
104.example: Banks are expected to dispense adequate credit at cheaper rates to farmers.

104.english_meaning: Something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of default.
104.hindi_meaning: संपार्श्विक प्रतिभूति / गिरवी रखने की संपत्ति
104.example: Since formal loans require collateral, many poor rural households are excluded from the credit network.

104.english_meaning: Lacking the quality or quantity required; insufficient for a purpose.
104.example: The formal credit delivery mechanism proved inadequate for the needs of rural poor.

104.english_meaning: Collected together from different individuals or groups to be shared and used by all.
104.hindi_meaning: संयुक्त रूप से एकत्रित (धन या संसाधन)
104.example: From the pooled money of the group, small loans are given to needy members.

104.english_meaning: A system of parts functioning together to achieve a specific result or process.
104.example: The formal credit delivery mechanism needs to be fully integrated into rural development.

104.english_meaning: Combined or coordinated to form a harmonious whole.
104.example: The credit system must be fully integrated into overall rural social development.

105.english_meaning: The process of becoming stronger and more confident, especially in controlling one's life and claiming one's rights.
105.example: Self-help groups have played a major role in the economic empowerment of rural women.

105.english_meaning: The lending of small amounts of money at low interest to new businesses in the developing world.
105.example: Micro-credit programmes help villagers start small businesses for income generation.

105.english_meaning: An act of assessing something or someone's value, quality, or performance.
105.example: A critical appraisal of the rural banking system reveals both successes and failures.

105.english_meaning: The action of organizing and mobilizing resources or people for a particular purpose, such as savings.
105.example: Formal financial institutions need to improve their culture of deposit mobilisation in rural areas.

105.english_meaning: Failure to fulfill an obligation, especially to repay a loan or appear in a law court.
105.hindi_meaning: ऋण चुकाने में असमर्थता / भुगतान चूक
105.example: Agriculture loan default rates have been chronically high across various states.

105.english_meaning: In a manner that persists for a long time or keeps recurring repeatedly.
105.example: Some rural banking sectors suffer from chronically high overdue loans.

105.english_meaning: A person or thing that prevents incompatible or antagonistic persons or things from coming into contact; a reserve stock.
105.example: The government maintains abundant buffer stocks of food grains for food security.

105.english_meaning: A deficit in a bank account caused by drawing more money than the account holds.
105.hindi_meaning: अधिलेखन / बैंक खाते से जमा राशि से अधिक निकालने की सुविधा
105.example: Jan-Dhan account holders are provided with overdraft facilities up to a certain limit.

105.english_meaning: Something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of a default.
105.example: Banks require proper collateral before approving large agricultural or housing loans.

105.english_meaning: Refrained from applying or enforcing a rule, penalty, or debt.
105.example: When crops fail completely, farmers often demand that their bank loans be waived.

105.english_meaning: The production of something, such as electricity, income, or employment opportunities.
105.example: Micro-credit programs are essential for income generation among poor rural families.

105.english_meaning: The action of providing or supplying something for use, or an arrangement made beforehand.
105.example: Financial credit provisions in rural areas help farmers purchase seeds and fertilizers.

106.english_meaning: The practice of using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully, often by saving.
106.hindi_meaning: मितव्ययिता या बचत करने की आदत
106.example: Opening bank accounts in rural areas has promoted the habit of thrift among people.

106.english_meaning: The action or process of distributing something or designating resources for a particular purpose.
106.example: Efficient allocation of financial resources is essential for economic development.

106.english_meaning: A system of parts working together in a machine or a process that leads to a particular result.
106.example: The mechanism through which goods reach different places depends on market channels.

106.english_meaning: Raw materials or primary agricultural products that can be bought and sold.
106.example: Agricultural marketing involves the distribution of various commodities across the country.

106.english_meaning: Action of manipulating something in a skillful manner or unauthorized changing of accounts to deceive.
106.example: Farmers previously suffered from faulty weighing and manipulation of accounts by traders.

106.english_meaning: The action or process of intervening to improve or prevent a situation.
106.example: Government intervention became necessary to regulate the activities of private traders.

106.english_meaning: To control or maintain the rate or speed of something, or to supervise through rules.
106.example: The first step was to regulate markets to create transparent marketing conditions.

106.english_meaning: Open, honest, and easily understood without secrets or hidden operations.
106.example: The policy helped create orderly and transparent marketing conditions for farmers.

106.english_meaning: A part or element of a larger whole, especially of a system or plan.
106.example: The second component of agricultural marketing is the provision of physical infrastructure.

106.english_meaning: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities needed for the operation of a society.
106.example: Physical infrastructure facilities include roads, railways, warehouses, and cold storages.

106.english_meaning: Large buildings where raw materials or manufactured goods may be stored before export or distribution.
106.example: Farmers need better warehouses and godowns to store their produce safely.

106.english_meaning: Lacking the quality or quantity required; insufficient for a particular purpose.
106.example: The current infrastructure facilities are quite inadequate to meet the growing demand.

107.english_meaning: People working together voluntarily for mutual social and economic benefit, such as farmers pooling resources.
107.example: The success of milk cooperatives transformed the rural economy of Gujarat.
Their great success is a testimony to hard work and unity.

107.english_meaning: A delay or setback that halts progress; an obstacle.
107.example: The project suffered a major setback due to a lack of funds.

107.english_meaning: A form of market intervention by the government to insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices.
107.example: The government announces the minimum support price before the sowing season.

107.english_meaning: A reserve of a commodity kept by a government to handle price fluctuations and shortages.
107.example: The Food Corporation of India maintains buffer stocks of wheat and rice.

107.english_meaning: Supported financially by the government so that prices are lower for consumers.
107.example: Poor families receive food grains at a subsidised rate through the public distribution system.

107.english_meaning: The action or process of intervening to improve a situation or correct a problem.
107.example: Government intervention is necessary to protect farmers from exploitation.

107.english_meaning: To be the strongest or main element; to have controlling power.
107.example: Private trade predominates agricultural markets despite state regulations.

107.hindi_meaning: आसन्न (जो बहुत जल्द होने वाला हो)
107.example: The need for regulatory intervention in the market is imminent.

107.english_meaning: Managing or running something principally for financial profit.
107.example: The commercialisation of agriculture allows farmers to grow cash crops for profit.

107.english_meaning: A union or association formed for mutual benefit, especially between organizations or countries.
107.example: Food chains form alliances with farmers to secure a steady supply of vegetables.

107.english_meaning: The effect or consequence that an action or decision will have.
107.example: We studied the economic implications of rising transport costs on food prices.

108.english_meaning: The action of obtaining or purchasing something, especially on behalf of a government or organization.
108.hindi_meaning: अधिप्राप्ति / क्रय करना (किसानों से सरकारी या निश्चित दामों पर फसल खरीदना)
108.example: The government announced assured procurement of wheat at pre-decided minimum support prices.

108.english_meaning: The process of diversifying or varying activities, products, or investments to reduce risk.
108.hindi_meaning: विविधीकरण (खेती के साथ-साथ अन्य क्षेत्रों या गतिविधियों को अपनाना)
108.example: Economic diversification helps farmers reduce their total dependence on crop farming.

108.english_meaning: A means of securing the necessities of life, such as income and employment.
108.example: Animal husbandry provides a sustainable livelihood for many rural families.

108.english_meaning: Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level without depleting natural resources.
108.example: The government aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices across the country.

108.english_meaning: Causes of severe trouble or suffering.
108.example: Rural development programs help poor families overcome the tribulations of poverty.

108.english_meaning: Connected or associated with something, especially in terms of related activities like farming.
108.hindi_meaning: संबद्ध / कृषि-संबद्ध (जैसे पशुपालन, मत्स्य पालन आदि)
108.example: Dairy farming and poultry are important allied activities of the agricultural sector.

108.english_meaning: Revoked or annulled a law or act by a legislative authority.
108.example: The controversial agricultural laws were later repealed by the Parliament.

108.english_meaning: Domestic farm animals kept for use or profit, such as cattle, sheep, and pigs.
108.example: Many marginal farmers depend on livestock for an alternative source of income.

108.english_meaning: The supply of water to land or crops to help growth, typically by means of channels.
108.example: Inadequate irrigation facilities during the Rabi season make crop cultivation difficult.

108.english_meaning: Completing or enhancing something, or providing extra help or income.
108.example: Non-farm employment acts as a supplementary source of income for rural households.

108.english_meaning: The people engaged in or available for work, either in a country or a particular company.
108.example: A major shift of the workforce from agriculture to non-farm sectors is necessary for growth.

108.english_meaning: To the exclusion of others; only and entirely.
108.hindi_meaning: विशेष रूप से / पूरी तरह से (केवल किसी एक पर निर्भर)
108.example: Rural families face greater risks when depending exclusively on farming for survival.

109.english_meaning: Filled with too many people or things, leaving no extra space.
109.example: As agriculture is already overcrowded, people need alternate employment in non-farm sectors.

109.english_meaning: Maintaining or supporting oneself at a minimum level, just enough to stay alive.
109.example: Some sectors are in subsistence, low productivity propositions.

109.english_meaning: The processing of raw materials from agriculture into value-added products.
109.example: The dynamic sub-sectors include agro-processing industries and food processing.

109.english_meaning: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.
109.example: Those sectors which have potential seriously lack infrastructure and other support.

109.english_meaning: Simple looms operated by hand, used for weaving cloth traditionally.
109.example: Traditional home-based industries like pottery, crafts, and handlooms need support.

109.english_meaning: Farm animals regarded as an asset, kept for use or profit (such as cattle, sheep, goats).
109.example: Livestock production provides increased stability in income and food security.

109.english_meaning: The state of being stable and unlikely to change or drop suddenly.
109.example: Livestock production provides increased stability in family income and food security.

109.english_meaning: Securing the necessities of life; a means of making a living.
109.example: The livestock sector provides alternate livelihood options to over 70 million farmers.

109.english_meaning: Domesticated birds kept for eggs or meat, such as chickens, ducks, and turkeys.
109.example: Poultry accounts for the largest share with 61 per cent in the livestock distribution.

109.english_meaning: A type of fertilizer produced by the action of earthworms decomposing organic waste.
109.example: Trained women are successfully making and selling vermicompost to earn money.

109.english_meaning: The lending of small amounts of money at low interest to new businesses in developing countries.
109.example: Many groups are creating savings by functioning like mini banks through a micro-credit system.

109.english_meaning: A person who sets up a business or businesses, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.
109.example: Talk to women entrepreneurs and discuss the details of their business in class.

110.english_meaning: Caused by or regarded as being caused by a particular thing.
110.hindi_meaning: कारण होना; किसी बात का श्रेय देना या किसी कारण से होना
110.example: The success of the project was attributed to teamwork.

121.english_meaning: To stop doing, operating, or providing something.
121.hindi_meaning: बीच में छोड़ देना या बंद करना
121.example: Many rural students discontinue their studies in the middle to join the workforce.

121.english_meaning: Notably large in size, amount, or extent.
121.example: A considerable section of urban youth is able to study in higher educational institutions.

121.english_meaning: Suitable or proper in the circumstances.
121.example: Urban people look for the appropriate job to suit their qualifications and skills.

121.english_meaning: A pass of an examination or an official completion of a course, training, or degree.
121.example: Candidates must possess the necessary qualifications to apply for the position.

122.english_meaning: The action of taking part in something, such as an activity or the workforce.
122.example: The participation of women in the workforce is lower in urban areas.

122.english_meaning: Actions that involve the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services for money.
122.example: Farming and trading are common economic activities in rural regions.

122.english_meaning: The state of having paid work.
122.example: Finding stable employment is crucial for economic development.

122.english_meaning: To cause someone to lose confidence or enthusiasm, or to persuade someone not to do something.
122.example: Traditional social norms sometimes discourage women from taking up jobs.

122.english_meaning: Producing or achieving a significant amount, especially in terms of goods, services, or value.
122.example: Many household chores done by women are not officially counted as productive work.

122.english_meaning: The act of guessing or calculating an amount, value, or importance to be lower than it actually is.
122.example: A narrow definition of work leads to the underestimation of female workers.

122.english_meaning: The process of preserving a condition or situation, or providing for the upkeep of a household.
122.example: Unpaid domestic labor contributes greatly to the maintenance of the household.

122.english_meaning: An indicator used for analyzing the employment situation in a country, calculated as the percentage of total population that is employed.
122.example: Any study of employment must start with a review of the worker-population ratios.

122.english_meaning: A business or company, or an organizational setup where work is carried out.
122.example: The status of a worker in an enterprise determines the quality of employment.

122.english_meaning: A measurable extent or aspect of a particular situation or problem.
122.example: Working conditions represent an important dimension of employment quality.

122.english_meaning: Employment on an irregular or intermittent basis, often without long-term job security or benefits.
122.example: Brick-making is often cited as a common form of casual work.

122.english_meaning: Groups of people living in the same place or sharing a particular characteristic or culture.
122.example: In some communities, social customs restrict women from stepping out for employment.

123.english_meaning: The process in which workers lose secure employment benefits and shift to informal or unprotected jobs.
123.hindi_meaning: अनौपचारिकीकरण (वह प्रक्रिया जिसमें कामगार अपनी सुरक्षित नौकरियाँ खो देते हैं और अनौपचारिक क्षेत्र में काम करने लगते हैं)
123.example: The rapid informalisation of the workforce poses new challenges for economic policy.

123.english_meaning: A business, firm, company, or similar organization.
123.example: He owns a small manufacturing enterprise in the industrial zone.

123.english_meaning: A means of securing the necessities of life, such as income or employment.
123.example: Agriculture remains the primary source of livelihood for millions of rural households.

123.english_meaning: Working for oneself rather than working for an employer or a specific company.
123.hindi_meaning: स्वयं-नियोजित या स्व-रोज़गार में लगे हुए
123.example: Shopkeepers and freelance consultants are generally self-employed workers.

123.english_meaning: The people engaged in or available for work, either in a country or a particular company.
123.example: A skilled and educated workforce is essential for rapid national development.

123.english_meaning: Workers who are casually engaged on a daily or periodic basis and paid wages for work done, without job security.
123.hindi_meaning: आकस्मिक दिहाड़ी मजदूर (जो अस्थायी रूप से काम करते हैं और दैनिक मजदूरी पाते हैं)
123.example: Many construction workers operate as casual wage labourers on various sites.

123.english_meaning: Money paid for work or a service rendered; payment or compensation.
123.example: The workers demanded fair remuneration for the overtime hours they put in.

123.english_meaning: Workers who are hired by an enterprise on a regular basis and receive regular wages or salaries.
123.hindi_meaning: नियमित वेतनभोगी कर्मचारी (जिन्हें नियमित रूप से वेतन मिलता है और रोजगार की निश्चितता होती है)
123.example: Government officers and corporate managers typically fall under regular salaried employees.

123.english_meaning: The way in which something is shared out among a group or spread over an area.
123.hindi_meaning: वितरण (चीजों या लोगों को आपस में बाँटने का ढंग)
123.example: The report illustrates the unequal distribution of wealth across different regions.

123.english_meaning: The state of being male or female, often used with reference to social and cultural differences.
123.hindi_meaning: लिंग (स्त्री या पुरुष होने की स्थिति)
123.example: Employment opportunities should be evaluated across different categories of gender and region.

123.english_meaning: An area or division, especially part of a country or the world having definable characteristics.
123.example: Economic growth rates can vary significantly from one region to another.

123.english_meaning: In, relating to, or characteristic of a town or city.
123.example: Urban workers often find employment in manufacturing, trade, and services.

124.english_meaning: Receiving a fixed regular payment, usually paid monthly, for employment.
124.hindi_meaning: वेतनभोगी (जिसे नियमित रूप से मासिक वेतन मिलता हो)
124.example: He secured a salaried job at a private hospital after completing his nursing degree.

124.english_meaning: Prepare and use land for crops or gardening.
124.example: Most farmers in rural areas own small plots of land and cultivate them independently.
Urban enterprises require workers on a regular basis to manage daily operations.

124.english_meaning: A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.
124.example: Men are found engaged in regular salaried employment in a greater proportion than women.

124.english_meaning: The way in which something is shared out among a group or spread over an area.
124.example: When we compare the distribution of the workforce in rural and urban areas, interesting trends emerge.

124.english_meaning: The people engaged in or available for work, either in a country or a particular company.
124.example: Government policies aim to improve the skill levels of the nation's workforce.

124.english_meaning: People offering something for sale, typically in the street.
124.example: Pavement vegetable vendors are considered self-employed workers in the economy.

124.english_meaning: People engaged or qualified in a profession, such as lawyers, doctors, or engineers.
124.example: Qualified professionals like doctors and lawyers often operate as self-employed individuals.

124.english_meaning: Experts in economics who study the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.
124.example: Economists point out that casual wage labourers are often the most economically vulnerable.

124.english_meaning: Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally/financially.
124.example: Casual wage labourers are identified as the most vulnerable category among workers due to irregular income.

124.english_meaning: Classes or divisions of people or things regarded as having particular shared characteristics.
124.example: Employment is generally divided into three main categories: self-employed, regular salaried, and casual wage.

124.english_meaning: A thing, especially a trend or fact, that shows the state or level of something.
124.example: Job security and health benefits are important economic indicators of the quality of employment.

125.english_meaning: The process through which the proportion of informal workers in the total workforce increases.
125.hindi_meaning: अनौपचारिकीकरण (कुल कार्यबल में अनौपचारिक श्रमिकों के अनुपात में वृद्धि की प्रक्रिया)
125.example: The rapid informalisation of the labor market poses new challenges for policymakers.

125.english_meaning: The sustained, concerted actions of policymakers and communities that promote the standard of living and economic health of a specific area.
125.example: In the course of economic development, labor flows from agriculture to industry.

125.english_meaning: To move from one region or country to another, often in search of work or better living conditions.
125.example: Workers often migrate from rural areas to urban centers in search of employment.

125.english_meaning: The action of becoming larger or more extensive.
125.example: The service sector entered a period of rapid expansion.

125.english_meaning: The way in which something is shared out among a group or spread over an area.
125.example: The table shows the distribution of workers across different industries.

125.english_meaning: The process of extracting stone or other materials from the earth.
125.hindi_meaning: उत्खनन या खदान से पत्थर निकालना
125.example: Mining and quarrying form a part of the primary industrial division.

125.english_meaning: The creation or production of goods on a large scale using machinery.
125.example: Manufacturing is a major component of the secondary sector.

125.english_meaning: The building of things like houses, offices, roads, and bridges.
125.example: Construction activities provide employment to a large number of unskilled workers.

125.english_meaning: Grouped or combined together for a common purpose or classification.
125.example: Economic activities can be clubbed into three major sectors.

125.english_meaning: The sector of an economy making direct use of natural resources, including agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.
125.hindi_meaning: प्राथमिक क्षेत्र (कृषि, खनन और संबंधित गतिविधियाँ)
125.example: The primary sector is the main source of employment for the majority of rural workers.

125.english_meaning: The sector of an economy that includes manufacturing, electricity, gas, water supply, and construction.
125.example: The secondary sector absorbs workers moving away from agriculture.

125.english_meaning: The service sector of the economy that provides commercial services to businesses and consumers.
125.example: Urban areas show high employment concentration in the tertiary sector.

126.english_meaning: The people engaged in or available for work, either in a country or a particular company or industry.
126.hindi_meaning: कार्यबल या काम करने वाले लोगों की कुल संख्या
126.example: About 60 per cent of the workforce in rural India depends on agriculture.

126.english_meaning: The sector of the economy concerned with manufacturing finished goods from raw materials.
126.hindi_meaning: द्वितीयक क्षेत्र (जिसमें विनिर्माण और उद्योग शामिल हैं)
126.example: The secondary sector provides employment to about one-third of the urban workforce.

126.english_meaning: The sector of the economy that produces services rather than products, also known as the tertiary sector.
126.example: About 61 per cent of urban workers are engaged in the service sector.

126.english_meaning: The sector of the economy involving the extraction and harvesting of natural products, such as agriculture and fishing.
126.hindi_meaning: प्राथमिक क्षेत्र (कृषि, वानिकी और मत्स्य पालन से जुड़ा क्षेत्र)
126.example: Both men and women workers are heavily concentrated in the primary sector.

126.english_meaning: The making of articles on a large scale using machinery.
126.example: Rural workers are also employed in manufacturing industries and construction.

126.english_meaning: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
126.example: You might have studied about the planning strategies in detail.

126.english_meaning: A thing, especially a trend or fact, that indicates the state or level of something.
126.example: Here we will look at two developmental indicators — growth of employment and GDP.

126.english_meaning: The total value of goods produced and services provided in a country during one year.
126.example: During the period 1950–2010, the Gross Domestic Product of India grew positively.

126.english_meaning: An irregular rising and falling in number or amount; a variation.
126.example: There was always fluctuation in the growth of GDP.

126.english_meaning: Causing someone to lose determination or confidence; discouraging.
126.example: Chart 6.3 points at another disheartening development in the late 1990s.

126.english_meaning: Becoming smaller, fewer, or worse; decreasing.
126.example: Employment growth started declining in the late 1990s.

126.english_meaning: A separate section or publication added to a newspaper or periodical.
126.hindi_meaning: अतिरिक्त परिशिष्ट या पत्रिका (अखबार का विशेष भाग)
126.example: Some newspapers devote an entire supplement in a day or every week for job opportunities.

127.english_meaning: An economic phenomenon where the overall gross domestic product (GDP) of a country increases while employment opportunities fail to grow at a similar pace.
127.hindi_meaning: बेरोज़गार विकास (ऐसी स्थिति जिसमें देश का सकल घरेलू उत्पाद तो बढ़ता है, लेकिन रोज़गार के अवसर पर्याप्त रूप से नहीं बढ़ते।)
127.example: The country experienced a period of jobless growth as output expanded without creating new jobs.

127.english_meaning: A fact or situation that is observed to happen, especially one whose cause or explanation is in question.
127.hindi_meaning: परिघटना (ऐसी घटना या स्थिति जिसका अध्ययन किया जाए।)
127.example: Migration from rural to urban areas is a common economic phenomenon.

127.english_meaning: A sign, statistic, or piece of information that shows the state or level of something.
127.hindi_meaning: सूचक या संकेतक (किसी स्थिति को दर्शाने वाला पैमाना या आँकड़ा।)
127.example: Employment rate is a vital economic indicator for the country.

127.english_meaning: Coming before something in time or order.
127.hindi_meaning: पूर्ववर्ती या पिछला (समय या क्रम में पहले आने वाला।)
127.example: As discussed in the preceding section, agricultural dependence has decreased.

127.english_meaning: Relating to cultivated land, farming, or a society centered on agriculture.
127.example: India has traditionally been an agrarian nation with a large rural population.

127.english_meaning: Means of securing the necessities of life, such as income or employment.
127.example: Millions of people depend on agriculture for their livelihood.

127.english_meaning: A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.
127.hindi_meaning: अनुपात या हिस्सा (कुल मात्रा में से किसी एक भाग का परिमाण।)
127.example: A large proportion of the workforce is engaged in the primary sector.

127.english_meaning: Of considerable importance, size, value, or extent.
127.hindi_meaning: पर्याप्त या महत्वपूर्ण (काफी बड़ा या भारी मात्रा में।)
127.example: There has been a substantial shift from farm work to non-farm work.

127.english_meaning: The sector of an economy making direct use of natural resources, including agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.
127.hindi_meaning: प्राथमिक क्षेत्र (कृषि, वानिकी और खनन जैसे प्राकृतिक संसाधनों से जुड़े कार्य।)
127.example: In 1972-73, the majority of the workforce was engaged in the primary sector.

127.english_meaning: The sector of an economy that transforms raw materials into goods, typically manufacturing and construction.
127.hindi_meaning: द्वितीयक क्षेत्र (विनिर्माण और उद्योगों से जुड़ा क्षेत्र, जिसमें कच्चे माल को वस्तुओं में बदला जाता है।)
127.example: The share of the secondary sector in the workforce has increased over the decades.

127.english_meaning: The tertiary sector of the economy that provides intangible services rather than physical goods, such as trade, transport, and education.
127.hindi_meaning: सेवा क्षेत्र (तृतीयक क्षेत्र जो वस्तुओं के बजाय सेवाएँ प्रदान करता है, जैसे व्यापार और परिवहन।)
127.example: The service sector is showing a promising future for the Indian workforce.

127.english_meaning: Of undisputed origin; genuine, reliable, and based on factual evidence.
127.hindi_meaning: प्रामाणिक या विश्वसनीय (सत्य और तथ्यों पर आधारित।)
127.example: The researchers used authentic data to analyze the growth of employment.

128.english_meaning: A state or condition of little or no growth, flow, or activity.
128.example: The stagnation of the secondary sector is a major concern for the economy.

128.english_meaning: The process of shifting from stable employment to casual or temporary wage work.
128.hindi_meaning: आकस्मिक मजوریकरण, अस्थायी रोजगार में वृद्धि
128.example: The casualisation of the workforce makes workers highly vulnerable to economic shocks.

128.english_meaning: Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or economically.
128.example: Casual laborers are often financially vulnerable due to a lack of job security.

128.english_meaning: A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen, especially one whose cause or explanation is in question.
128.example: Economists are trying to explain the phenomenon of jobless growth in the country.

128.english_meaning: The sector of the economy concerned with manufacturing and construction.
128.example: The secondary sector includes industries and manufacturing units.

128.english_meaning: The sector of the economy involving agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.
128.example: A large portion of India's workforce is still engaged in the primary sector.

128.english_meaning: The sector of the economy that produces services rather than end products, such as IT, trade, and transport.
128.example: The services sector has shown significant growth over the last few decades.

128.english_meaning: Working for oneself as a freelance owner of a business rather than for an employer.
128.hindi_meaning: स्व-रोज़गार, खुद का काम करने वाला
128.example: Self-employment continues to be the major employment provider in India.

128.english_meaning: An economic phenomenon in which an economy experiences growth while maintaining an unchanged level of employment.
128.example: Jobless growth happens when the output of goods and services increases without a proportional rise in jobs.

128.english_meaning: Experts in economics who study the production and distribution of resources, goods, and services.
128.example: Economists analyze trends in employment patterns to understand labor market shifts.

128.english_meaning: Relating to or situated at the edge or margin; in agriculture, having little profit or productivity.
128.example: A marginal farmer often struggles to make ends meet with limited land resources.

128.english_meaning: Produced or created, especially in terms of employment, power, or revenue.
128.example: New economic policies helped in generating additional employment opportunities.

129.english_meaning: The process by which the proportion of informal workers in the total workforce increases over time.
129.hindi_meaning: अनौपचारीकरण (वह प्रक्रिया जिसमें कुल कार्यबल में अनौपचारिक कामगारों का अनुपात बढ़ जाता है)
129.example: The rapid informalisation of the Indian workforce raises serious concerns about job security.

129.english_meaning: A means of securing the necessities of life, such as income and employment.
129.example: Agriculture remains the major source of livelihood for millions of people in rural areas.

129.english_meaning: Contemplated or planned as a future possibility; expected.
129.hindi_meaning: परिकल्पित (भविष्य के लिए योजना बनाना या कल्पना करना)
129.example: It was envisaged that industrialisation would improve the standard of living for workers.

129.english_meaning: Becoming progressively worse in quality or condition.
129.example: Economists argue that the overall quality of employment has been deteriorating over the years.

129.english_meaning: A payment given by an employer to an employee when they leave service after a long period of employment.
129.hindi_meaning: उपदान (सेवा निवृत्ति या नौकरी छोड़ने पर नियोक्ता द्वारा दिया जाने वाला धन)
129.example: Many informal sector workers do not receive benefits like provident fund and gratuity.

129.english_meaning: Business organizations, offices, or public sector enterprises.
129.example: All public sector establishments are classified under the formal sector.

129.english_meaning: The sector comprising public sector enterprises and private sector enterprises employing 10 or more hired workers.
129.example: Workers in the formal sector enjoy legal protection, regular income, and social security benefits.

129.english_meaning: The sector that includes all other enterprises, self-employed persons, and casual wage labourers without hired workers.
129.example: Millions of farmers and construction workers form a major part of the informal sector.

129.english_meaning: Workers who are employed on a daily or intermittent basis and do not have regular jobs or security.
129.example: Construction workers and headload workers often work as casual wage labourers.

129.english_meaning: Measures providing protection to workers against risks such as illness, unemployment, old age, and workplace injury.
129.example: Trade unions bargain with employers for better wages and social security measures.

129.english_meaning: Arranging items or people in categories according to shared qualities or characteristics.
129.example: Economists use specific criteria for classifying the workforce into formal and informal sectors.

129.english_meaning: Be a part of a whole; make up or form something.
129.example: Women constitute only about one-sixth of the formal sector workforce in India.

130.english_meaning: The sector consisting of public enterprises, private establishments, and workers who get social security benefits and regular employment.
130.hindi_meaning: औपचारिक क्षेत्र (वह क्षेत्र जहाँ कर्मचारियों को सामाजिक सुरक्षा लाभ और नियमित रोजगार मिलता है)
130.example: Those who are working in the formal sector enjoy social security benefits.

130.english_meaning: The sector comprising private enterprises, temporary workers, and street vendors who lack job security and formal benefits.
130.hindi_meaning: अनौपचारिक क्षेत्र (वह क्षेत्र जिसमें अस्थायी कामगार और छोटे उद्यम शामिल होते हैं, जिन्हें सामाजिक सुरक्षा नहीं मिलती)
130.example: About 89 per cent of the workforce in India is engaged in the informal sector.

130.english_meaning: Government protection and provisions (such as pensions, provident fund, and medical benefits) provided to workers.
130.hindi_meaning: सामाजिक सुरक्षा (कर्मचारियों को मिलने वाले लाभ जैसे पेंशन, भविष्य निधि और चिकित्सीय सहायता)
130.example: Those who are working in the formal sector enjoy social security benefits.

130.english_meaning: Contemplated or planned as a future possibility; foreseen.
130.hindi_meaning: परिकल्पना की गई (भविष्य के लिए योजना बनाना या सोचना)
130.example: Developmental planning envisaged that more workers would become formal sector workers over time.

130.english_meaning: A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.
130.example: The proportion of workers engaged in the informal sector was expected to dwindle.

130.english_meaning: To diminish gradually in size, amount, or strength.
130.example: The planners hoped that the share of the informal sector would dwindle as the economy grew.

130.english_meaning: The people engaged in or available for work, either in a country or a particular company.
130.example: In 2019–20 there were about 535 million workers in the total Indian workforce.

130.english_meaning: To roughly calculate or judge the value, number, quantity, or extent of something.
130.example: Can you estimate the percentage of people employed in the informal sectors?

130.english_meaning: The way in which something is shared out among a group or spread over an area.
130.example: The chart gives the distribution of workforce in formal and informal sectors.

130.english_meaning: The advertising and offering of goods for sale, especially on the street.
130.example: Road side vending is an increasing variety of informal sector employment.

130.english_meaning: The condition of having paid work; a job.
130.example: Informal sector employment constitutes the vast majority of jobs in India.

130.english_meaning: The state of a country or region in terms of the production and consumption of goods and services and the supply of money.
130.example: Developmental planning envisaged that as the economy grows, more workers would join the formal sector.

131.english_meaning: The process by which a growing number of workers move from secure formal employment to insecure informal jobs without benefits or legal protection.
131.hindi_meaning: अनौपचारीकरण (वह प्रक्रिया जिसमें कामगार सुरक्षित औपचारिक नौकरियों से असुरक्षित अनौपचारिक क्षेत्र की ओर धकेले जाते हैं)
131.example: The sudden closure of textile mills led to a rapid increase in the informalisation of labor in Ahmedabad.

131.english_meaning: Successful in material terms; flourishing financially and economically.
131.example: Ahmedabad was once a prosperous city driven by its large textile industry.

131.english_meaning: The state of being free from danger, threat, or anxiety about the future, such as financial or job security.
131.hindi_meaning: सुरक्षा, संरक्षण (जैसे सामाजिक सुरक्षा या आय की सुरक्षा)
131.example: Workers in the organized sector enjoy better social security schemes for their health and old age.

131.english_meaning: An organized association of workers formed to protect and further their rights and interests.
131.example: A strong trade union represented the mill workers in industrial disputes and welfare activities.

131.english_meaning: A period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced.
131.example: The closure of major industries caused a severe economic recession in the city.

131.english_meaning: The part of an economy that is neither taxed, monitored by any form of government, nor included in any gross national product.
